5.76.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
tathānyadapi tatrāsti bhāskaratritayaṃ śubham ..
yaistuṣṭaistriṣu lokeṣu mānavo muktimāpnuyāt .. 1 ..
5.76.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
तथान्यदपि तत्रास्ति भास्करत्रितयं शुभम् ..
यैस्तुष्टैस्त्रिषु लोकेषु मानवो मुक्तिमाप्नुयात् .. 1 ..
5.76.m: Sūta said: / Likewise, there is another auspicious triad of suns there, / by whose pleasure a human being can attain liberation across the three worlds:

5.76.s:
muṇḍīraṃ prathamaṃ tatra kālapriyaṃ tathāparam ..
mūlasthānaṃ tṛtīyaṃ ca sarvavyādhivināśanam .. 2 ..
5.76.d:
मुण्डीरं प्रथमं तत्र कालप्रियं तथापरम् ..
मूलस्थानं तृतीयं च सर्वव्याधिविनाशनम् .. 2 ..
5.76.m: Muṇḍīra is the first there, Kālapriya is the second, / and Mūlasthāna is the third, destroying all diseases.

5.76.s:
tatra saṃkramate sūryo muṃḍīre rajanīkṣaye ..
kālapriye ca madhyāhne mūlasthāne kṣapāgame .. 3 ..
5.76.d:
तत्र संक्रमते सूर्यो मुंडीरे रजनीक्षये ..
कालप्रिये च मध्याह्ने मूलस्थाने क्षपागमे .. 3 ..
5.76.m: The sun transfers to Muṇḍīra at the end of the night, / to Kālapriya at midday, and to Mūlasthāna at the arrival of night.

5.76.s:
tasminkāle naro bhaktyā paśyedapyekamevaca ..
kṛtakṣaṇo naro mokṣaṃ satyaṃ yāti na saṃśayaḥ .. 4 ..
5.76.d:
तस्मिन्काले नरो भक्त्या पश्येदप्येकमेवच ..
कृतक्षणो नरो मोक्षं सत्यं याति न संशयः .. 4 ..
5.76.m: If a man with devotion looks upon even one [of them] at that time, / that fortunate man truly attains liberation, without a doubt.

5.76.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
muṃḍīraḥ pūrvadigbhāge dharitryāḥ śrūyate kila ..
madhye kālapriyo devo mūlasthānaṃ tadantare .. 5 ..
5.76.d:
.. ऋषय ऊचुः .. ..
मुंडीरः पूर्वदिग्भागे धरित्र्याः श्रूयते किल ..
मध्ये कालप्रियो देवो मूलस्थानं तदन्तरे .. 5 ..
5.76.m: The seers said: / Muṇḍīra is heard to be in the eastern direction of the earth, / the god Kālapriya in the middle, and Mūlasthāna between them.

5.76.s:
tatkathaṃ te trayastatra saṃjātāḥ sūta bhāskarāḥ ..
hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre sarvaṃ no brūhi vistarāt .. 6 ..
5.76.d:
तत्कथं ते त्रयस्तत्र संजाताः सूत भास्कराः ..
हाटकेश्वरजे क्षेत्रे सर्वं नो ब्रूहि विस्तरात् .. 6 ..
5.76.m: How then did those three suns arise there / in the sacred field born of Hāṭakeśvara? Tell us everything in detail, O Sūta.

5.76.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
asti sāgaraparyaṃte viṭaṃkapuramuttamam ..
samudravīcisaṃsaktaproccaprākāramaṇḍanam .. 7 ..
5.76.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
अस्ति सागरपर्यंते विटंकपुरमुत्तमम् ..
समुद्रवीचिसंसक्तप्रोच्चप्राकारमण्डनम् .. 7 ..
5.76.m: Sūta said: / On the edge of the ocean there is an excellent city called Viṭaṅkapura, / adorned with very lofty ramparts touched by the waves of the sea.

5.76.s:
tatrābhūdbrāhmaṇaḥ kaścitkuṣṭhavyādhisamanvitaḥ ..
pūrvakarmavipākena yauvanesamupasthite .. 8 ..
5.76.d:
तत्राभूद्ब्राह्मणः कश्चित्कुष्ठव्याधिसमन्वितः ..
पूर्वकर्मविपाकेन यौवनेसमुपस्थिते .. 8 ..
5.76.m: There was a certain brahmin there afflicted with the disease of leprosy / due to the ripening of past deeds, just as youth arrived.

5.76.s:
tasya bhāryā'bhavatsādhvī kulīnā śīlamaṃḍanā ..
tathābhūtamapi prāyaḥ sā paśyati yathā smaram .. 9 ..
5.76.d:
तस्य भार्याऽभवत्साध्वी कुलीना शीलमंडना ..
तथाभूतमपि प्रायः सा पश्यति यथा स्मरम् .. 9 ..
5.76.m: His wife was a chaste woman of noble family, adorned with good character; / though he was in such a state, she generally viewed him as if he were the god of love.

5.76.s:
auṣadhāni vicitrāṇi mahārghyāṇyapi cādade ..
tadarthamupalepāṃśca pathyāni vividhāni ca .. 6.76.10 ..
5.76.d:
औषधानि विचित्राणि महार्घ्याण्यपि चाददे ..
तदर्थमुपलेपांश्च पथ्यानि विविधानि च .. 6.76.10 ..
5.76.m: She obtained various costly medicines / for his sake, as well as unguents and various wholesome foods.

5.76.s:
tathā bhiṣagvarānnityamānināya ca sādaram ..
tadarthe na guṇastasya tathāpi syāccharīrajaḥ .. 11 ..
5.76.d:
तथा भिषग्वरान्नित्यमानिनाय च सादरम् ..
तदर्थे न गुणस्तस्य तथापि स्याच्छरीरजः .. 11 ..
5.76.m: Likewise, she continually brought the best physicians with great respect / for his sake, yet no bodily improvement occurred for him.

5.76.s:
yathāyathā sa gṛhṇāti bheṣajāni dvijottamāḥ ..
kuṣṭhena sarvagātreṣu vyāpyate ca tathātathā .. 12 ..
5.76.d:
यथायथा स गृह्णाति भेषजानि द्विजोत्तमाः ..
कुष्ठेन सर्वगात्रेषु व्याप्यते च तथातथा .. 12 ..
5.76.m: The more remedies he took, O best of twice-born, / the more all his limbs became overrun with leprosy.

5.76.s:
athaivaṃ vartamānasya tasya vipravarasya ca ..
gṛhe'tithiḥ samāyātaḥ kaścitpāṃthaḥ śramānvitaḥ .. 13 ..
5.76.d:
अथैवं वर्तमानस्य तस्य विप्रवरस्य च ..
गृहेऽतिथिः समायातः कश्चित्पांथः श्रमान्वितः .. 13 ..
5.76.m: Now, while that excellent brahmin was living in this manner, / a certain weary traveler came as a guest to his house.

5.76.s:
atha vipraṃ gṛhaṃ prāptaṃ dṛṣṭvā tasya satī priyā ..
ajñātamapisadbhaktyā sūpacārairatoṣayat .. 14 ..
5.76.d:
अथ विप्रं गृहं प्राप्तं दृष्ट्वा तस्य सती प्रिया ..
अज्ञातमपिसद्भक्त्या सूपचारैरतोषयत् .. 14 ..
5.76.m: Seeing the brahmin arrived at the house, his virtuous and beloved wife / pleased him with excellent hospitalities out of genuine devotion, even though he was a stranger.

5.76.s:
atha taṃ snātamācāṃtaṃ kṛtāhāraṃ dvijottamam ..
viśrāntaṃ śayane vipraḥ provāca sa gṛhādhipaḥ .. 15 ..
5.76.d:
अथ तं स्नातमाचांतं कृताहारं द्विजोत्तमम् ..
विश्रान्तं शयने विप्रः प्रोवाच स गृहाधिपः .. 15 ..
5.76.m: Then, after that best of twice-born had bathed, sipped water, eaten his meal, / and rested on a couch, the brahmin master of the house spoke to him—

5.76.s:
tejo'nvitaṃ yathā bhānuṃ rūpaudāryaguṇānvitam ..
yauvane vartamānaṃ ca mūrtaṃ kāmamivāparam .. 16 ..
5.76.d:
तेजोऽन्वितं यथा भानुं रूपौदार्यगुणान्वितम् ..
यौवने वर्तमानं च मूर्तं काममिवापरम् .. 16 ..
5.76.m: endowed with splendor like the sun, possessed of beauty, generosity, and virtues, / dwelling in his youth, like a second god of love incarnate.

5.76.s:
.. kuṣṭhyuvāca .. ..
kuta āgamyate vipra kva yāsyasi vadā'dhunā ..
evaṃ lāvaṇyayukto'pi kimekākī yathārtibhāk .. 17 ..
5.76.d:
.. कुष्ठ्युवाच .. ..
कुत आगम्यते विप्र क्व यास्यसि वदाऽधुना ..
एवं लावण्ययुक्तोऽपि किमेकाकी यथार्तिभाक् .. 17 ..
5.76.m: The leper said: / Whence do you come, O brahmin? Where will you go? Tell me now. / Though endowed with such loveliness, why are you alone, as if suffering distress?

5.76.s:
.. pathika uvāca .. ..
asti kāntīpurīnāma puraṃdarapurī yathā ..
susthitaiḥ sevitā nityaṃ janairdharmavratānvitaiḥ .. 18 ..
5.76.d:
.. पथिक उवाच .. ..
अस्ति कान्तीपुरीनाम पुरंदरपुरी यथा ..
सुस्थितैः सेविता नित्यं जनैर्धर्मव्रतान्वितैः .. 18 ..
5.76.m: The traveler said: / There is a city named Kāntīpurī, like the city of Indra, / constantly inhabited by well-settled people endowed with religious observances.

5.76.s:
tasyāmahaṃ kṛtāvāso gṛhasthāśramamāvahan ..
grastaḥ kuṣṭhena raudreṇa yathā tvaṃ dvijasattama .. 19 ..
5.76.d:
तस्यामहं कृतावासो गृहस्थाश्रममावहन् ..
ग्रस्तः कुष्ठेन रौद्रेण यथा त्वं द्विजसत्तम .. 19 ..
5.76.m: Making my residence there and maintaining the householder's stage of life, / I was seized by terrible leprosy, just as you are, O best of twice-born.

5.76.s:
tataḥ śrutaṃ mayā tāvatpurāṇe skāndasaṃjñite ..
bhāskaratritayaṃ bhūmau sarvavyādhivināśanam .. 6.76.20 ..
5.76.d:
ततः श्रुतं मया तावत्पुराणे स्कान्दसंज्ञिते ..
भास्करत्रितयं भूमौ सर्वव्याधिविनाशनम् .. 6.76.20 ..
5.76.m: Then I heard of the triad of suns on the earth, which destroys all diseases, / as recorded in the Purāṇa known as Skānda.

5.76.s:
tato nirvedamāpanno bheṣajaiḥ kleśitaściram ..
kṣāraiścāmlaiḥ kaṣāyaiśca kaṭukairatha tiktakaiḥ .. 21 ..
5.76.d:
ततो निर्वेदमापन्नो भेषजैः क्लेशितश्चिरम् ..
क्षारैश्चाम्लैः कषायैश्च कटुकैरथ तिक्तकैः .. 21 ..
5.76.m: Thereupon, having become dejected and afflicted for a long time by medicines— / by alkaline, sour, astringent, pungent, and bitter ones—

5.76.s:
tato viniścayaṃ citte kṛtvā gṛhya dhanaṃ mahat ..
muṇḍīrasvāminaṃ gatvā sthitastasyaiva sannidhau .. 22 ..
5.76.d:
ततो विनिश्चयं चित्ते कृत्वा गृह्य धनं महत् ..
मुण्डीरस्वामिनं गत्वा स्थितस्तस्यैव सन्निधौ .. 22 ..
5.76.m: and making a firm resolve in my mind, I took great wealth, / went to Lord Muṇḍīra, and remained right in his presence.

5.76.s:
tataḥ prātaḥ samutthāya nityaṃ paśyāmi taṃ vibhum ..
pūjayāmi svaśaktyā ca praṇamāmi tataḥ param.. 23 ..
5.76.d:
ततः प्रातः समुत्थाय नित्यं पश्यामि तं विभुम् ..
पूजयामि स्वशक्त्या च प्रणमामि ततः परम्.. 23 ..
5.76.m: Then, rising in the morning, I continually looked upon that lord; / I worshipped him to the best of my ability and then bowed down to him.

5.76.s:
sūryavāre viśeṣeṇa nirāhāro yatendriyaḥ ..
karomi jāgaraṃ rātrau gītavāditraniḥsvanaiḥ .. 24 ..
5.76.d:
सूर्यवारे विशेषेण निराहारो यतेन्द्रियः ..
करोमि जागरं रात्रौ गीतवादित्रनिःस्वनैः .. 24 ..
5.76.m: Especially on Sunday, without food and with restrained senses, / I kept vigil at night with the sounds of songs and musical instruments.

5.76.s:
tataḥ saṃvatsarasyāṃte taṃ praṇamya dinādhipam ..
kālapriyaṃ tataḥ paścācchraddhayā parayā yutaḥ .. 25 ..
5.76.d:
ततः संवत्सरस्यांते तं प्रणम्य दिनाधिपम् ..
कालप्रियं ततः पश्चाच्छ्रद्धया परया युतः .. 25 ..
5.76.m: Then, at the end of a year, having bowed down to that lord of the day, / and endowed with supreme faith, [I went] after that to Kālapriya...

5.76.s:
tenaiva vidhinā vipra tasyāpi divaseśituḥ ..
pūjāṃ karomi madhyāhne śraddhā pūtena cetasā .. 26 ..
5.76.d:
तेनैव विधिना विप्र तस्यापि दिवसेशितुः ..
पूजां करोमि मध्याह्ने श्रद्धा पूतेन चेतसा .. 26 ..
5.76.m: By that very rite, O brahmin, with a mind purified by faith, / I performed worship of that Lord of the Day too at midday.

5.76.s:
tato'pi vatsarasyāṃte taṃ praṇamyātha śaktitaḥ ..
mūlasthānaṃ gato devamaparasyāṃ diśi sthitam .. 27 ..
5.76.d:
ततोऽपि वत्सरस्यांते तं प्रणम्याथ शक्तितः ..
मूलस्थानं गतो देवमपरस्यां दिशि स्थितम् .. 27 ..
5.76.m: Then at the end of the year, having bowed down to him according to my capacity, / I went to the deity Mūlasthāna situated in the western quarter.

5.76.s:
tenaiva vidhinā pūjā tasyāpi vihitā mayā ..
saṃdhyākāle dvijaśreṣṭha yāvatsaṃvatsaraṃ sthitaḥ .. 28 ..
5.76.d:
तेनैव विधिना पूजा तस्यापि विहिता मया ..
संध्याकाले द्विजश्रेष्ठ यावत्संवत्सरं स्थितः .. 28 ..
5.76.m: By that very rite worship was performed by me of him as well / at the twilight hour, O best of the twice-born, remaining there for a year.

5.76.s:
tataḥ saṃvatsarasyāṃte svapne māṃ bhāskaro'bravīt ..
sametya prahasanvipraḥ saṃprahṛṣṭena cetasā .. 29 ..
5.76.d:
ततः संवत्सरस्यांते स्वप्ने मां भास्करोऽब्रवीत् ..
समेत्य प्रहसन्विप्रः संप्रहृष्टेन चेतसा .. 29 ..
5.76.m: Then at the end of the year, the Sun approached me in a dream / and spoke with an exceedingly delighted mind, smiling, O brahmin:

5.76.s:
parituṣṭo'smi te vipra karmaṇā'nena bhaktitaḥ ..
mamārādhanajenaiva tasmātkuṣṭhaṃ prayātu te .. 6.76.30 ..
5.76.d:
परितुष्टोऽस्मि ते विप्र कर्मणाऽनेन भक्तितः ..
ममाराधनजेनैव तस्मात्कुष्ठं प्रयातु ते .. 6.76.30 ..
5.76.m: ‘I am well-pleased with you, O brahmin, through this rite performed with devotion, / born of worship offered to me; therefore let your leprosy depart!

5.76.s:
gaccha śīghraṃ dvijaśreṣṭha śrāṃto'si nijamaṃdiram ..
paśya baṃdhujanaṃ sarvaṃ sotkaṇṭhaṃ tatkṛte sthitam .. 31 ..
5.76.d:
गच्छ शीघ्रं द्विजश्रेष्ठ श्रांतोऽसि निजमंदिरम् ..
पश्य बंधुजनं सर्वं सोत्कण्ठं तत्कृते स्थितम् .. 31 ..
5.76.m: Go quickly to your own home, O best of the twice-born; you are fatigued; / behold all your kinsfolk waiting with longing for your sake.

5.76.s:
tvayā hṛtaṃ purā rukmaṃ brāhmaṇasya mahātmanaḥ ..
tena karmavipākena kuṣṭhavyādhirupasthitaḥ .. 32..
5.76.d:
त्वया हृतं पुरा रुक्मं ब्राह्मणस्य महात्मनः ..
तेन कर्मविपाकेन कुष्ठव्याधिरुपस्थितः .. 32..
5.76.m: Formerly, gold belonging to a noble-souled brahmin was stolen by you; / by the ripening of that deed, the disease of leprosy befell you.

5.76.s:
sa mayā nāśitastubhyaṃ prahṛṣṭenādhunā dvija ..
etajjñātvā na kartavyaṃ suvarṇaharaṇaṃ punaḥ .. 33 ..
5.76.d:
स मया नाशितस्तुभ्यं प्रहृष्टेनाधुना द्विज ..
एतज्ज्ञात्वा न कर्तव्यं सुवर्णहरणं पुनः .. 33 ..
5.76.m: It has now been destroyed by me for you, well-pleased, O twice-born; / knowing this, the theft of gold should never again be committed.

5.76.s:
dṛśyante ye narā loke kuṣṭhavyādhisamākulāḥ ..
suvarṇaharaṇaṃ sarvaistaiḥ kṛtaṃ pāpakarmabhiḥ .. 34 ..
5.76.d:
दृश्यन्ते ये नरा लोके कुष्ठव्याधिसमाकुलाः ..
सुवर्णहरणं सर्वैस्तैः कृतं पापकर्मभिः .. 34 ..
5.76.m: Those men who are seen in the world afflicted with the disease of leprosy— / the theft of gold was committed by all those evil-doers.

5.76.s:
tasmāddeyaṃ yathāśaktyā na steyaṃ kanakaṃ budhaiḥ ..
icchadbhiḥ paramaṃ saukhyaṃ svaśarīrasya śāśvatam .. 35 ..
5.76.d:
तस्माद्देयं यथाशक्त्या न स्तेयं कनकं बुधैः ..
इच्छद्भिः परमं सौख्यं स्वशरीरस्य शाश्वतम् .. 35 ..
5.76.m: Therefore, gold should be given according to one’s capacity, not stolen by the wise / who desire supreme, enduring happiness for their own bodies.’

5.76.s:
evamuktvā sahasrāṃśustataścādarśanaṃ gataḥ ..
ahaṃ ca vismayāviṣṭaḥ protthitaḥ śayanāddrutam .. .. 36 ..
5.76.d:
एवमुक्त्वा सहस्रांशुस्ततश्चादर्शनं गतः ..
अहं च विस्मयाविष्टः प्रोत्थितः शयनाद्द्रुतम् .. .. 36 ..
5.76.m: Having spoken thus, the Thousand-Rayed One then vanished from sight, / and I, overcome with wonder, quickly arose from my bed.

5.76.s:
yāvatpaśyāmi dehaṃ svaṃ kuṣṭhavyādhiparicyutam ..
dvādaśārkaprabhaṃ divyaṃ yathā tvaṃ paśyase dvija .. 37 ..
5.76.d:
यावत्पश्यामि देहं स्वं कुष्ठव्याधिपरिच्युतम् ..
द्वादशार्कप्रभं दिव्यं यथा त्वं पश्यसे द्विज .. 37 ..
5.76.m: When I looked at my own body, it was freed from the disease of leprosy, / divine, shining like twelve suns, just as you behold, O twice-born.

5.76.s:
tasmāttvamapi vipreṃdra bhaktyā tadbhāskaratrayam ..
anena vidhinā paśya yena kuṣṭhaṃ praśāmyati ..38..
5.76.d:
तस्मात्त्वमपि विप्रेंद्र भक्त्या तद्भास्करत्रयम् ..
अनेन विधिना पश्य येन कुष्ठं प्रशाम्यति ..38..
5.76.m: Therefore, you too, O chief of brahmins, behold with devotion that triad of Suns / by this procedure, by which leprosy is cured.

5.76.s:
kimauṣadhaiḥ kimāhāṃraiḥ kaṭukairapi yojitaiḥ ..
sarvavyādhipraṇāśeśe sthite'sminbhāskaratraye .. 39 ..
5.76.d:
किमौषधैः किमाहांरैः कटुकैरपि योजितैः ..
सर्वव्याधिप्रणाशेशे स्थितेऽस्मिन्भास्करत्रये .. 39 ..
5.76.m: What use are medicines, what use diets even when prepared with bitter herbs, / when this triad of Suns, capable of destroying all diseases, is present?

5.76.s:
svasti te'stu gamiṣyāmi sāṃprataṃ tāṃ purīṃ prati ..
gṛhe'dya tava viśrāṃto yathā vipra nije gṛhe .. 6.76.40 ..
5.76.d:
स्वस्ति तेऽस्तु गमिष्यामि सांप्रतं तां पुरीं प्रति ..
गृहेऽद्य तव विश्रांतो यथा विप्र निजे गृहे .. 6.76.40 ..
5.76.m: May it be well with you! I shall depart now toward that city; / I have rested today in your house, O brahmin, as in my own house.’

5.76.s:
evamuktaḥ sa pāṃthena tena vipraḥ sa kuṣṭhabhāk ..
vīkṣāṃcakre tato vaktraṃ svapatnyā duḥkhasaṃyutaḥ .. 41 ..
5.76.d:
एवमुक्तः स पांथेन तेन विप्रः स कुष्ठभाक् ..
वीक्षांचक्रे ततो वक्त्रं स्वपत्न्या दुःखसंयुतः .. 41 ..
5.76.m: Spoken to thus by that traveler, the brahmin afflicted with leprosy / then looked upon the face of his own wife, filled with sorrow.

5.76.s:
sā'bravīdyuktamuktaṃ te pāṃthenānena vallabha ..
tasmāttatra drutaṃ gaccha yatra tadbhāskaratrayam .. 42 ..
5.76.d:
साऽब्रवीद्युक्तमुक्तं ते पांथेनानेन वल्लभ ..
तस्मात्तत्र द्रुतं गच्छ यत्र तद्भास्करत्रयम् .. 42 ..
5.76.m: She said: ‘What was spoken to you by this traveler is right, O beloved; / therefore go quickly there where that triad of Suns is.

5.76.s:
ahaṃ tvayā samaṃ tatra śuśrūṣāniratā satī ..
gamiṣyāmi na saṃdehastasmādgaccha drutaṃ vibho .. 43 ..
5.76.d:
अहं त्वया समं तत्र शुश्रूषानिरता सती ..
गमिष्यामि न संदेहस्तस्माद्गच्छ द्रुतं विभो .. 43 ..
5.76.m: I, devoted to serving you as a faithful wife, / will go there along with you, without a doubt; therefore go quickly, O lord.’

5.76.s:
evamuktastayā so'tha vittamādāya bhūriśaḥ ..
prasthitaḥ kāṃtayā sārdhaṃ muṇḍīrasvāminaṃ prati .. 44 ..
5.76.d:
एवमुक्तस्तया सोऽथ वित्तमादाय भूरिशः ..
प्रस्थितः कांतया सार्धं मुण्डीरस्वामिनं प्रति .. 44 ..
5.76.m: Spoken to thus by her, he then took abundant wealth / and set out along with his beloved toward Muṇḍīrasvāmin:

5.76.s:
pratijñayā gamiṣyāmi draṣṭuṃ taddevatātrayam..
muṃḍīraṃ kālanāthaṃ ca mūla sthānaṃ ca bhāskaram .. 45 ..
5.76.d:
प्रतिज्ञया गमिष्यामि द्रष्टुं तद्देवतात्रयम्..
मुंडीरं कालनाथं च मूल स्थानं च भास्करम् .. 45 ..
5.76.m: ‘With a solemn vow I shall go to behold that triad of deities— / Muṇḍīra, Kālanātha, and the Sun at Mūlasthāna.’

5.76.s:
tataḥ kṛcchreṇa mahatā kuṣṭhavyādhisamākulaḥ ..
hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre saṃprāptaḥ sa dvijottamāḥ .. 46 ..
5.76.d:
ततः कृच्छ्रेण महता कुष्ठव्याधिसमाकुलः ..
हाटकेश्वरजे क्षेत्रे संप्राप्तः स द्विजोत्तमाः .. 46 ..
5.76.m: Then with great difficulty, afflicted with the disease of leprosy, / he arrived at the sacred field born of Hāṭakeśvara, O best of the twice-born.

5.76.s:
taddṛṣṭvā sumahatkṣetraṃ tāpasaughaniṣevitam ..
nirviṇṇaḥ kuṣṭharogeṇa pathi śrāṃto'bravītpriyām .. 47 ..
5.76.d:
तद्दृष्ट्वा सुमहत्क्षेत्रं तापसौघनिषेवितम् ..
निर्विण्णः कुष्ठरोगेण पथि श्रांतोऽब्रवीत्प्रियाम् .. 47 ..
5.76.m: Beholding that very great sacred field frequented by hosts of ascetics, / despondent from the disease of leprosy and fatigued on the road, he said to his beloved:

5.76.s:
ahaṃ nirvedamāpanno rogeṇātha bubhukṣayā ..
muṇḍīrasvāminaṃ yāvanna śakromi prasarpitum ..48..
5.76.d:
अहं निर्वेदमापन्नो रोगेणाथ बुभुक्षया ..
मुण्डीरस्वामिनं यावन्न शक्रोमि प्रसर्पितुम् ..48..
5.76.m: ‘I have fallen into despair on account of disease and hunger; / I am not able to crawl as far as Muṇḍīrasvāmin.

5.76.s:
tasmādatraiva dehaṃ svaṃ vihāsyāmi na saṃśayaḥ ..
tvaṃ gaccha svagṛhaṃ kāṃte sārthamāsādya śobhanam ..49..
5.76.d:
तस्मादत्रैव देहं स्वं विहास्यामि न संशयः ..
त्वं गच्छ स्वगृहं कांते सार्थमासाद्य शोभनम् ..49..
5.76.m: Therefore I will abandon my own body right here, without doubt; / you, O beloved, go to your own home, having found a good caravan.’

5.76.s:
.. patnyuvāca .. ..
abhukte tvayi no bhuktaṃ kadācitkāṃta vai mayā ..
ekāṃte'pi mahābhāga na suptaṃ jāgrati tvayi .. 6.76.50 ..
5.76.d:
.. पत्न्युवाच .. ..
अभुक्ते त्वयि नो भुक्तं कदाचित्कांत वै मया ..
एकांतेऽपि महाभाग न सुप्तं जाग्रति त्वयि .. 6.76.50 ..
5.76.m: The wife said: / ‘When you had not eaten, O beloved, I certainly never ate; / even in solitary privacy, O highly fortunate one, I did not sleep while you were awake.

5.76.s:
tasmādetanmahākṣetraṃ saṃprāpya tvāṃ vyavasthitam..
paralokāya saṃtyajya kathaṃ gacchāmyahaṃ gṛham .. 51 ..
5.76.d:
तस्मादेतन्महाक्षेत्रं संप्राप्य त्वां व्यवस्थितम्..
परलोकाय संत्यज्य कथं गच्छाम्यहं गृहम् .. 51 ..
5.76.m: Therefore, having reached this great sacred field, abandoning you / who are prepared for the next world, how can I go home?

5.76.s:
darśayiṣye mukhaṃ teṣāṃ tvayā hīnā ahaṃ katham ..
bāṃdhavānāṃ gurūṇāṃ ca anyeṣāṃ sudṛdā mapi ..52..
5.76.d:
दर्शयिष्ये मुखं तेषां त्वया हीना अहं कथम् ..
बांधवानां गुरूणां च अन्येषां सुदृदा मपि ..52..
5.76.m: Bereft of you, how shall I show my face to them— / to relatives, elders, and even to other friends?

5.76.s:
tasmāttvayā samaṃ nātha pravekṣyāmi hutāśanam ..
snehapāśavinirbaddhā satyenātmānamālabhe..53..
5.76.d:
तस्मात्त्वया समं नाथ प्रवेक्ष्यामि हुताशनम् ..
स्नेहपाशविनिर्बद्धा सत्येनात्मानमालभे..53..
5.76.m: Therefore, along with you, O lord, I will enter the fire; / bound by the cords of affection, I touch myself with truth.

5.76.s:
yāvatastava saṃjātā upavāsā mahāmate..
tāvaṃtaśca tathāsmākaṃ kathaṃ gacchāmi tadgṛham..54..
5.76.d:
यावतस्तव संजाता उपवासा महामते..
तावंतश्च तथास्माकं कथं गच्छामि तद्गृहम्..54..
5.76.m: As many fasts as have occurred for you, O wise one, / so many have occurred for us; how can I go to that home?’

5.76.s:
evaṃ tasyā viditvā sa niścayaṃ brāhmaṇastadā ..
citiṃ kṛtvā tu dāhārthaṃ tayā sārdhe tato'viśat .. ..55..
5.76.d:
एवं तस्या विदित्वा स निश्चयं ब्राह्मणस्तदा ..
चितिं कृत्वा तु दाहार्थं तया सार्धे ततोऽविशत् .. ..55..
5.76.m: Knowing her resolve thus, the brahmin then / constructed a funeral pyre for burning and entered it together with her.

5.76.s:
bhāskaraṃ manasi dhyātvā yāvadagniṃ samādade ..
tāvatpaśyati cāgrasthaṃ sudīptaṃ puruṣatrayam..56..
5.76.d:
भास्करं मनसि ध्यात्वा यावदग्निं समाददे ..
तावत्पश्यति चाग्रस्थं सुदीप्तं पुरुषत्रयम्..56..
5.76.m: Meditating in his mind upon the Sun, as he took up the fire, / he beheld three blazing men standing before him.

5.76.s:
taddṛṣṭvā vismayāviṣṭaḥ ka ete puruṣāstrayaḥ..
na kadācinmayā dṛṣṭā īdṛktejaḥsamanvitāḥ .. 57 ..
5.76.d:
तद्दृष्ट्वा विस्मयाविष्टः क एते पुरुषास्त्रयः..
न कदाचिन्मया दृष्टा ईदृक्तेजःसमन्विताः .. 57 ..
5.76.m: Beholding them, filled with wonder, [he thought]: ‘Who are these three men? / Never have I seen anyone endowed with such splendor!’

5.76.s:
.. puruṣā ūcuḥ .. ..
mā tvaṃ mṛtyupathaṃ gaccha kṛtvā vairāgyamākulaḥ ..
vyāvṛtya svagṛhaṃ gaccha sva bhāryāsahito dvija .. 58 ..
5.76.d:
.. पुरुषा ऊचुः .. ..
मा त्वं मृत्युपथं गच्छ कृत्वा वैराग्यमाकुलः ..
व्यावृत्य स्वगृहं गच्छ स्व भार्यासहितो द्विज .. 58 ..
5.76.m: The men said: / ‘Do not go upon the path of death, perturbed, having embraced renunciation! / Turn back and go to your own home accompanied by your wife, O twice-born!’

5.76.s:
.. brāhmaṇa uvāca .. ..
pratijñāya mayā pūrva gṛhaṃ muktaṃ nijaṃ yataḥ ..
muṇḍīrasvāminaṃ dṛṣṭvā tathā'nyaṃ kālavallabham .. .. 59 ..
5.76.d:
.. ब्राह्मण उवाच .. ..
प्रतिज्ञाय मया पूर्व गृहं मुक्तं निजं यतः ..
मुण्डीरस्वामिनं दृष्ट्वा तथाऽन्यं कालवल्लभम् .. .. 59 ..
5.76.m: The brahmin said: / ‘Because having made a vow earlier, my own home was abandoned by me, / that after seeing Muṇḍīrasvāmin, and likewise the other, Kālavallabha,

5.76.s:
mūlasthānaṃ ca kartavyaṃ tataḥ sasyaprabhakṣaṇam ..
so'haṃ tānavilokyātha kathaṃ gacchāmi mandiram ..
bhakṣayāmi tathā sasyaṃ tena tyakṣyāmi jīvitam.. 6.76.60 ..
5.76.d:
मूलस्थानं च कर्तव्यं ततः सस्यप्रभक्षणम् ..
सोऽहं तानविलोक्याथ कथं गच्छामि मन्दिरम् ..
भक्षयामि तथा सस्यं तेन त्यक्ष्यामि जीवितम्.. 6.76.60 ..
5.76.m: and Mūlasthāna, the consumption of grain was to be done; / so without seeing them, how can I go to my dwelling / and eat grain? Therefore I shall give up my life.’

5.76.s:
.. puruṣā ūcuḥ .. ..
vayaṃ te bhāskarā brahmaṃstrayo'traiva samāgatāḥ ..
tvadbhaktyākṛṣṭamanaso brūhi kiṃ karavāmahe .. 61 .. ..
5.76.d:
.. पुरुषा ऊचुः .. ..
वयं ते भास्करा ब्रह्मंस्त्रयोऽत्रैव समागताः ..
त्वद्भक्त्याकृष्टमनसो ब्रूहि किं करवामहे .. 61 .. ..
5.76.m: The men said: / ‘We are those three Suns, O brahmin, arrived right here, / our minds drawn by your devotion; speak, what shall we do?’

5.76.s:
.. brāhmaṇa uvāca .. ..
yadi yūyaṃ samāyātāḥ svayameva mamāṃtikam ..
trayo'pi bhāskarā nāśameṣa kuṣṭhaḥ pragacchatu .. 62 ..
5.76.d:
.. ब्राह्मण उवाच .. ..
यदि यूयं समायाताः स्वयमेव ममांतिकम् ..
त्रयोऽपि भास्करा नाशमेष कुष्ठः प्रगच्छतु .. 62 ..
5.76.m: The brahmin said: / ‘If you three Suns have indeed come into my presence of your own accord, / then let this leprosy go to destruction!

5.76.s:
tathā'traiva sadā stheyaṃ kṣetre yuṣmābhireva hi ..
sāṃnidhyaṃ triṣu lokeṣu gantavyaṃ ca yathā purā .. 63 ..
5.76.d:
तथाऽत्रैव सदा स्थेयं क्षेत्रे युष्माभिरेव हि ..
सांनिध्यं त्रिषु लोकेषु गन्तव्यं च यथा पुरा .. 63 ..
5.76.m: Likewise, you should remain forever in this sacred field itself, / and your presence should be accessible in the three worlds just as before.’

5.76.s:
.. bhāskarā ūcuḥ .. ..
evaṃ vipra kariṣyāmaḥ sthāsyāmo 'tra sadā vayam ..
tvaṃ cāpi roganirmuktaḥ sukhaṃ prāpsyasyanuttamam .. 64 ..
5.76.d:
.. भास्करा ऊचुः .. ..
एवं विप्र करिष्यामः स्थास्यामो ऽत्र सदा वयम् ..
त्वं चापि रोगनिर्मुक्तः सुखं प्राप्स्यस्यनुत्तमम् .. 64 ..
5.76.m: The Suns said: / ‘We shall do so, O brahmin; we will remain here forever, / and you, freed from disease, will attain unsurpassed happiness.

5.76.s:
prāsādatritayaṃ tasmādasmadarthaṃ nirūpaya ..
yena trikālamāsādya gacchāmaḥ saṃnidhiṃ dvija .. 65 ..
5.76.d:
प्रासादत्रितयं तस्मादस्मदर्थं निरूपय ..
येन त्रिकालमासाद्य गच्छामः संनिधिं द्विज .. 65 ..
5.76.m: Therefore, assign a triad of temples for our sake, / so that, arriving at the three times of day, we enter into presence, O twice-born.’

5.76.s:
evamuktvā tu te sarve gatāścāddarśanaṃ tataḥ ..
so'pi paśyati kāyaṃ svaṃ yāvadrogavivarjitam .. 66 ..
5.76.d:
एवमुक्त्वा तु ते सर्वे गताश्चाद्दर्शनं ततः ..
सोऽपि पश्यति कायं स्वं यावद्रोगविवर्जितम् .. 66 ..
5.76.m: Having spoken thus, they all vanished from sight then, / and he too beheld his body freed from disease.

5.76.s:
dvādaśārka pratīkāśaṃ sarvalakṣaṇalakṣitam ..
tataḥ provāca tāṃ bhāryāṃ vinayāvanatāṃ sthitām .. 67 ..
5.76.d:
द्वादशार्क प्रतीकाशं सर्वलक्षणलक्षितम् ..
ततः प्रोवाच तां भार्यां विनयावनतां स्थिताम् .. 67 ..
5.76.m: shining like twelve suns and marked with all auspicious marks. / Then he spoke to his wife, who stood bowed in humility: 67

5.76.s:
paśya tvaṃ subhrūrme gātraṃ yādṛgrūpaṃ punaḥ sthitam ..
prasādāddevadevasya bhāskarasyāṃśumālinaḥ .. 68 ..
5.76.d:
पश्य त्वं सुभ्रूर्मे गात्रं यादृग्रूपं पुनः स्थितम् ..
प्रसादाद्देवदेवस्य भास्करस्यांशुमालिनः .. 68 ..
5.76.m: "Look, fair-browed one, at how my body has become whole once again / through the grace of the god of gods, the sun-god, the garlanded with rays! 68

5.76.s:
so'hamatra sthito nityaṃ pūjayiṣyāmi bhāskaram ..
na yāsyāmi punaḥ sadma satyametanmayoditam..69..
evamuktvā sa viprendrastasminkṣetre suśobhane..
prāsādatritayaṃ ramyaṃ nirmame bhaktisaṃyutaḥ..6.76.7...
muṇḍīrasvāminaścaikamanyatkālapriyasya ca..
mūlasthānasya cānyattu satpatākāvibhūṣitam..7...
5.76.d:
सोऽहमत्र स्थितो नित्यं पूजयिष्यामि भास्करम् ..
न यास्यामि पुनः सद्म सत्यमेतन्मयोदितम्..69..
एवमुक्त्वा स विप्रेन्द्रस्तस्मिन्क्षेत्रे सुशोभने..
प्रासादत्रितयं रम्यं निर्ममे भक्तिसंयुतः..6.76.7...
मुण्डीरस्वामिनश्चैकमन्यत्कालप्रियस्य च..
मूलस्थानस्य चान्यत्तु सत्पताकाविभूषितम्..7...
5.76.m:
Remaining here, I shall constantly worship the sun; / I shall not return home. This truth is spoken by me." 69
Having spoken thus, that best of brahmins, filled with devotion, / built three delightful temples in that most lovely sacred field: 70
one for Muṇḍīrasvāmin, another for Kālapriya, / and another for Mūlasthāna, adorned with noble banners. 71

5.76.s:
trayāṇāmapi teṣāṃ tu sādhvarcāḥ śāstrasūcitāḥ..
sthāpayāmāsa sūryāṇāṃ hastārke sūryavāsare ... 72 ..
5.76.d:
त्रयाणामपि तेषां तु साध्वर्चाः शास्त्रसूचिताः..
स्थापयामास सूर्याणां हस्तार्के सूर्यवासरे ... 72 ..
5.76.m: And in them he installed proper images of those three suns, / as prescribed by the scriptures, on a Sunday when the sun was in Hasta. 72

5.76.s:
tatastāḥ puṣpadhūpādyaiḥ samabhyarcya ciraṃ dvijaḥ ..
trisaṃdhyaṃ kramaśaḥ prāpto dehāṃte bhāskarālayam .. 73 ..
5.76.d:
ततस्ताः पुष्पधूपाद्यैः समभ्यर्च्य चिरं द्विजः ..
त्रिसंध्यं क्रमशः प्राप्तो देहांते भास्करालयम् .. 73 ..
5.76.m: Then, having long worshipped them at the three junctures of the day / with flowers, incense, and the like, the brahmin gradually attained the sun-god's abode at the end of his body. 73

5.76.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
evaṃ te tatra saṃjātāstrayo'pi dvijasattamāḥ ..
bhāskarā bhaktalokasya sarvavyādhivināśakāḥ .. 74 ..
5.76.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
एवं ते तत्र संजातास्त्रयोऽपि द्विजसत्तमाः ..
भास्करा भक्तलोकस्य सर्वव्याधिविनाशकाः .. 74 ..
5.76.m: Sūta said: / Thus arose those three suns there, O best of brahmins, / destroying all diseases for their devoted worshippers. 74

5.76.s:
yastānpaśyati kāle sve yathokte sūraryavāsare ..
sa vāṃchitām̐llabhetkāmāndurlabhānapi mānavaiḥ ..75..
5.76.d:
यस्तान्पश्यति काले स्वे यथोक्ते सूरर्यवासरे ..
स वांछिताम्̐ल्लभेत्कामान्दुर्लभानपि मानवैः ..75..
5.76.m: Whoever beholds them at their proper time, as prescribed on a Sunday, / attains his desired wishes, even those difficult for humans to attain. 75

5.76.s: iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe hāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye muṃḍīrakālapriyamūlasthānapratiṣṭhāvarṇanaṃnāma ṣaṭsaptatitamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 76 .. .. cha ..
5.76.d: इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे हाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये मुंडीरकालप्रियमूलस्थानप्रतिष्ठावर्णनंनाम षट्सप्ततितमोऽध्यायः .. 76 .. .. छ ..
5.76.m: Thus ends the seventy-sixth chapter, named 'The Description of the Consecration of Muṇḍīra, Kālapriya, and Mūlasthāna', in the Praise of the Sacred Field of Hāṭakeśvara, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [part] of the glorious Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses. 76

5.77.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
yadetadbhavatā proktaṃ tatra tau parameśvarau ..
umāmaheśvarau sūta hariścandreṇa bhūbhujā .. 1 ..
5.77.d:
.. ऋषय ऊचुः .. ..
यदेतद्भवता प्रोक्तं तत्र तौ परमेश्वरौ ..
उमामहेश्वरौ सूत हरिश्चन्द्रेण भूभुजा .. 1 ..
5.77.m: The seers said: / Regarding what you said about those two supreme lords, / Umā and Maheśvara, O Sūta, being established by King Hariścandra, 1

5.77.s:
kṛtau kathayasītyevaṃ vedimadhyaṃ samāśritau ..
utānyau sthāpitau tatra camatkārapurāṃtikam .. 2 ..
5.77.d:
कृतौ कथयसीत्येवं वेदिमध्यं समाश्रितौ ..
उतान्यौ स्थापितौ तत्र चमत्कारपुरांतिकम् .. 2 ..
5.77.m: as you narrate, seated in the middle of the sacrificial altar, / or whether two others were installed there near Camatkārapura: 2

5.77.s:
vedimadhyagatau nityaṃ pārvatīparameśvarau ..
etatsaṃśrūyate sūta vivāhaḥ prāgabhūttayoḥ ..
oṣadhiprasthamāsādya puraṃ hima vataḥ priyam .. 3 ..
5.77.d:
वेदिमध्यगतौ नित्यं पार्वतीपरमेश्वरौ ..
एतत्संश्रूयते सूत विवाहः प्रागभूत्तयोः ..
ओषधिप्रस्थमासाद्य पुरं हिम वतः प्रियम् .. 3 ..
5.77.m: Pārvatī and Parameśvara ever seated in the middle of the altar— / it is traditionally heard, O Sūta, that their wedding previously took place / when they reached Oṣadhiprastha, the dear city of the Himavat. 3

5.77.s:
atra naḥ saṃśayo jātaḥ śraddheyamapi te vacaḥ..
śrutvā kiṃ vā bhramaste'yaṃ kiṃ vā'smākaṃ prakīrtaya .. 4 ..
5.77.d:
अत्र नः संशयो जातः श्रद्धेयमपि ते वचः..
श्रुत्वा किं वा भ्रमस्तेऽयं किं वाऽस्माकं प्रकीर्तय .. 4 ..
5.77.m: On this point doubt has arisen for us, though your word is trustworthy. / Having heard this, tell us: is this a delusion of yours, or of ours? 4

5.77.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
nāsmākaṃ vibhramo jāto yuṣmākaṃ tu dvijottamāḥ ..
paraṃ yatkāraṇaṃ kṛtsnaṃ tadbravīmi nibodhyatām .. 5 ..
5.77.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
नास्माकं विभ्रमो जातो युष्माकं तु द्विजोत्तमाः ..
परं यत्कारणं कृत्स्नं तद्ब्रवीमि निबोध्यताम् .. 5 ..
5.77.m: Sūta said: / No delusion has arisen for me, but rather for you, O best of brahmins! / Yet I shall explain the entire reason; listen attentively. 5

5.77.s:
ya eṣa oṣadhiprasthe vivāhaḥ prāgabhū ttayoḥ ..
umātrinetrayo ramyaḥ sarvadevapramodakṛt .. 6 ..
5.77.d:
य एष ओषधिप्रस्थे विवाहः प्रागभू त्तयोः ..
उमात्रिनेत्रयो रम्यः सर्वदेवप्रमोदकृत् .. 6 ..
5.77.m: That charming wedding of the two, Umā and the Three-Eyed Lord, / which took place previously in Oṣadhiprastha and delighted all the gods, 6

5.77.s:
vaivasvate'ntare pūrvaṃ saṃjāto dvijasattamāḥ ..
saptamasya tu vikhyāto yuṣmākaṃ vidito'tra yaḥ .. 7 ..
5.77.d:
वैवस्वतेऽन्तरे पूर्वं संजातो द्विजसत्तमाः ..
सप्तमस्य तु विख्यातो युष्माकं विदितोऽत्र यः .. 7 ..
5.77.m: took place in the Vaivasvata interval of old, O best of brahmins, / in the seventh [manvantara]—the famous one that is known to you here. 7

5.77.s:
hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre yaścodvāhastayorabhūt ..
svāyaṃbhuvamanorādye sa saṃjātaḥ suvistaraḥ .. 8 ..
5.77.d:
हाटकेश्वरजे क्षेत्रे यश्चोद्वाहस्तयोरभूत् ..
स्वायंभुवमनोराद्ये स संजातः सुविस्तरः .. 8 ..
5.77.m: And the marriage of the two that occurred in the sacred field of Hāṭakeśvara / took place with great circumstance in the first [manvantara], that of Svāyambhuva Manu. 8

5.77.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
vivāha oṣadhiprasthe yaḥ purā samabhūttayoḥ ..
pārvatīharayoḥ sūta so'smābhirvistarācchrutaḥ .. 9 ..
5.77.d:
.. ऋषय ऊचुः .. ..
विवाह ओषधिप्रस्थे यः पुरा समभूत्तयोः ..
पार्वतीहरयोः सूत सोऽस्माभिर्विस्तराच्छ्रुतः .. 9 ..
5.77.m: The seers said: / The wedding of the two, Pārvatī and Hara, which took place in ancient times / at Oṣadhiprastha, O Sūta, has been heard by us at length. 9

5.77.s:
hāṭakeśvaraje kṣetre dakṣayajñe manohare ..
vivāho vṛṣayānasya manau svāyaṃbhuve purā .. 6.77.10 ..
5.77.d:
हाटकेश्वरजे क्षेत्रे दक्षयज्ञे मनोहरे ..
विवाहो वृषयानस्य मनौ स्वायंभुवे पुरा .. 6.77.10 ..
5.77.m: The wedding of the Bull-Riding Lord in the sacred field of Hāṭakeśvara / during Dakṣa's lovely sacrifice in the time of Svāyambhuva Manu of old— 10

5.77.s:
so'smākaṃ kīrtanīyaśca tvayā sūtakulodvaha ..
vistareṇa yathā vṛttaḥ etanna kautukaṃ param .. 11 ..
5.77.d:
सोऽस्माकं कीर्तनीयश्च त्वया सूतकुलोद्वह ..
विस्तरेण यथा वृत्तः एतन्न कौतुकं परम् .. 11 ..
5.77.m: that must be narrated to us by you, O upholder of the lineage of the Sūtas, / at length, just as it occurred. This is a matter of great curiosity to us! 11

5.77.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
atra vaḥ kīrtayiṣyāmi sarvapātakanāśanam ..
vivāhasamayaṃ samyagdevadevasya śūlinaḥ .. 12 ..
5.77.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
अत्र वः कीर्तयिष्यामि सर्वपातकनाशनम् ..
विवाहसमयं सम्यग्देवदेवस्य शूलिनः .. 12 ..
5.77.m: Sūta said: / Here I shall tell you, destroying all sins, / the full occasion of the wedding of the spear-wielding god of gods. 12

5.77.s:
brahmaṇo dakṣiṇāṃguṣṭhāddakṣaḥ prācetaso'bhavat ..
śatāni pañca kanyānāṃ tasya jātāni ca dvijāḥ .. 13 ..
5.77.d:
ब्रह्मणो दक्षिणांगुष्ठाद्दक्षः प्राचेतसोऽभवत् ..
शतानि पञ्च कन्यानां तस्य जातानि च द्विजाः .. 13 ..
5.77.m: From the right thumb of Brahmā, Dakṣa, son of Pracetas, was born. / And five hundred daughters were born to him, O brahmins. 13

5.77.s:
tāsāṃ jyeṣṭhatamā sādhvī satīnāma śucismitā ..
babhūva kanyakā sarvairguṇairyuktā''yatekṣaṇā . .. 14 ..
5.77.d:
तासां ज्येष्ठतमा साध्वी सतीनाम शुचिस्मिता ..
बभूव कन्यका सर्वैर्गुणैर्युक्ता'ऽयतेक्षणा . .. 14 ..
5.77.m: The eldest of them was a virtuous maiden named Satī, pure-smiling, / endowed with all virtues and possessing long eyes. 14

5.77.s:
na devī na ca gaṃdharvī nāsurī na ca nāgajā ..
tādṛgrūpā'bhavaccānyā yādṛśī sā sumadhyamā .. 15 ..
atha tāṃ pradadau dakṣaḥ patnyarthaṃ śūla pāṇaye ..
prārthitāṃ bahuśo yatnātsaspṛhāya spṛhānvitām ...6..
5.77.d:
न देवी न च गंधर्वी नासुरी न च नागजा ..
तादृग्रूपाऽभवच्चान्या यादृशी सा सुमध्यमा .. 15 ..
अथ तां प्रददौ दक्षः पत्न्यर्थं शूल पाणये ..
प्रार्थितां बहुशो यत्नात्सस्पृहाय स्पृहान्विताम् ...6..
5.77.m:
Neither goddess, nor Gandharva woman, nor Asura woman, nor maiden of the Nāgas / was of such form as that slender-waisted lady was. 15
Then Dakṣa gave her as wife to the spear-bearer, / she who had been earnestly sought after repeatedly, giving the eager maiden to him who was full of desire. 16

5.77.s:
tataḥ puṇyatamaṃ kṣetraṃ kanyādānasya sa kṣamam ..
saṃdhyāya sasutāmātyaḥ sabhṛtyaḥ samupasthitaḥ .. 17 ..
5.77.d:
ततः पुण्यतमं क्षेत्रं कन्यादानस्य स क्षमम् ..
संध्याय ससुतामात्यः सभृत्यः समुपस्थितः .. 17 ..
5.77.m: Then, having contemplated the most meritorious sacred field suitable for giving away the daughter, / he arrived with his daughter, ministers, and attendants. 17

5.77.s:
tataścodvāhayogyāni vasuni vividhānyapi ..
ānayāmāsa bhūrīṇi māṃgalyāni viśeṣataḥ .. 18 ..
5.77.d:
ततश्चोद्वाहयोग्यानि वसुनि विविधान्यपि ..
आनयामास भूरीणि मांगल्यानि विशेषतः .. 18 ..
5.77.m: Then he brought various wealth suitable for a wedding, / abundant and especially auspicious. 18

5.77.s:
atha caitrasya śuklasya nakṣatre bhagadaivate ..
trayodaśyāṃ dine bhānoḥ samāyāto maheśvaraḥ .. 19 ..
5.77.d:
अथ चैत्रस्य शुक्लस्य नक्षत्रे भगदैवते ..
त्रयोदश्यां दिने भानोः समायातो महेश्वरः .. 19 ..
5.77.m: Then, during the bright fortnight of Caitra, under the constellation ruled by Bhaga, / on the thirteenth day, a Sunday, Maheśvara arrived, 19

5.77.s:
sarvaiḥ suragaṇaiḥ sārdhaṃ devaviṣṇupuraḥsaraiḥ..
ādityairvasubhī rudrairaśvibhyāṃ ca tathā'paraiḥ .. 6.77.20 ..
5.77.d:
सर्वैः सुरगणैः सार्धं देवविष्णुपुरःसरैः..
आदित्यैर्वसुभी रुद्रैरश्विभ्यां च तथाऽपरैः .. 6.77.20 ..
5.77.m: accompanied by all the hosts of gods led by the god Viṣṇu, / by the Ādityas, Vasus, Rudras, and the two Aśvins, as well as others, 20

5.77.s:
siddhaiḥ sādhyagaṇairbhūtaiḥ pretairvaināyakaistathā ..
gandharvaiścāraṇaughaiśca guhyakairyakṣarākṣasaiḥ .. 21 ..
5.77.d:
सिद्धैः साध्यगणैर्भूतैः प्रेतैर्वैनायकैस्तथा ..
गन्धर्वैश्चारणौघैश्च गुह्यकैर्यक्षराक्षसैः .. 21 ..
5.77.m: by Siddhas, hosts of Sādhyas, Bhūtas, Pretas, and attendants of Vināyaka, / by Gandharvas, multitudes of Cāraṇas, Guhyakas, Yakṣas, and Rākṣasas. 21

5.77.s:
etasminnaṃtare dakṣaḥ saṃprahṛṣṭatanūruhaḥ ..
prayayau saṃmukhastasya yuktaḥ sarvaiḥ suhṛdgaṇaiḥ .. 22 ..
5.77.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे दक्षः संप्रहृष्टतनूरुहः ..
प्रययौ संमुखस्तस्य युक्तः सर्वैः सुहृद्गणैः .. 22 ..
5.77.m: Meanwhile Dakṣa, the hairs of his body bristling with delight, / went out to meet him together with all his hosts of kinsmen, 22

5.77.s:
vādyamānairmahāvādyaiḥ sūtamāgadhabandibhiḥ ..
paṭhadbhiḥ sarvato'nekairgāyadbhirgāyanaistathā .. 23 ..
5.77.d:
वाद्यमानैर्महावाद्यैः सूतमागधबन्दिभिः ..
पठद्भिः सर्वतोऽनेकैर्गायद्भिर्गायनैस्तथा .. 23 ..
5.77.m: while great musical instruments were played, and sūtas, māgadhas, and bards / recited on all sides, and numerous singers sang. 23

5.77.s:
tataḥ sarve surāstatra svayaṃ dakṣeṇa pūjitāḥ ..
yathāśreṣṭhaṃ yathājyeṣṭhamupaviṣṭā yathākramam ..
parivāryākhilāṃ vediṃ maṃḍapāṃtaravartinīm .. 24 ..
5.77.d:
ततः सर्वे सुरास्तत्र स्वयं दक्षेण पूजिताः ..
यथाश्रेष्ठं यथाज्येष्ठमुपविष्टा यथाक्रमम् ..
परिवार्याखिलां वेदिं मंडपांतरवर्तिनीम् .. 24 ..
5.77.m: Then all the gods, honoured there by Dakṣa himself, / sat down in proper order according to rank and seniority, / encircling the entire altar situated inside the pavilion. 24

5.77.s:
tataḥ pitāmahaṃ prāha dakṣaḥ prītipuraḥsaram ..
praṇipatya tvayā karma kāryaṃ vaivāhikaṃ vibhoḥ .. 25 ..
5.77.d:
ततः पितामहं प्राह दक्षः प्रीतिपुरःसरम् ..
प्रणिपत्य त्वया कर्म कार्यं वैवाहिकं विभोः .. 25 ..
5.77.m: Then Dakṣa bowed down and spoke to the Grandfather with love: / "You must perform the wedding ritual of the Lord, 25

5.77.s:
svayameva sutā'smākaṃ yena syātsubhagā satī ..
putra pautravatī nityaṃ suśīlā pativallabhā .. 26 ..
5.77.d:
स्वयमेव सुताऽस्माकं येन स्यात्सुभगा सती ..
पुत्र पौत्रवती नित्यं सुशीला पतिवल्लभा .. 26 ..
5.77.m: in person, so that our daughter Satī may be fortunate, / ever endowed with sons and grandsons, well-behaved, and dear to her husband." 26

5.77.s:
bāḍhamityeva so'pyuktvā prahṛṣṭenāṃtarātmanā ..
samutthāya tataścakre kṛtyamarhaṇapūrvakam .. 27 ..
5.77.d:
बाढमित्येव सोऽप्युक्त्वा प्रहृष्टेनांतरात्मना ..
समुत्थाय ततश्चक्रे कृत्यमर्हणपूर्वकम् .. 27 ..
5.77.m: Saying, "So be it!" with an inner soul full of joy, / he rose and then performed the rites preceded by ceremonial worship. 27

5.77.s:
saṃpradānakriyāṃ kṛtvā tatraiva vidhipūrvakam ..
tato hastagrahaṃ tābhyāṃ mithaścakre yathākramam ..
mātṝṇāṃ purato vedhāḥ satīśābhyāṃ yathocitam .. 28 ..
5.77.d:
संप्रदानक्रियां कृत्वा तत्रैव विधिपूर्वकम् ..
ततो हस्तग्रहं ताभ्यां मिथश्चक्रे यथाक्रमम् ..
मातॄणां पुरतो वेधाः सतीशाभ्यां यथोचितम् .. 28 ..
5.77.m: Having performed the ceremony of giving away the bride right there according to rule, / the Creator then duly caused the joining of hands to be done between the two / before the mothers, as was proper for Satī and the Lord. 28

5.77.s:
atha vediṃ samāsādya gṛhyoktavidhinā'khilam ..
agnikāryaṃ yathoddiṣṭaṃ cakārātha suvistaram .. 29 ..
5.77.d:
अथ वेदिं समासाद्य गृह्योक्तविधिनाऽखिलम् ..
अग्निकार्यं यथोद्दिष्टं चकाराथ सुविस्तरम् .. 29 ..
5.77.m: Then, approaching the altar according to the rules of the domestic ritual manuals, / he carried out all the rites of fire in detail as prescribed. 29

5.77.s:
yathāyathā sa ramyāṇi vīkṣateṃ'gāni kautukāt ..
satyāḥ pitāmaho hṛṣṭaḥ kāmārto'bhūttathātathā .. 6.77.30 ..
5.77.d:
यथायथा स रम्याणि वीक्षतेंऽगानि कौतुकात् ..
सत्याः पितामहो हृष्टः कामार्तोऽभूत्तथातथा .. 6.77.30 ..
5.77.m: As he looked with curiosity at the lovely limbs of Satī, / the delighted Grandfather became increasingly overcome with desire. 30

5.77.s:
tenaikaṃ vadanaṃ muktvā tasyā vastrāvaguṃṭhitam ..
vīkṣitā'tismarārtena yathā kaścinna buddhyate .. 31 ..
5.77.d:
तेनैकं वदनं मुक्त्वा तस्या वस्त्रावगुंठितम् ..
वीक्षिताऽतिस्मरार्तेन यथा कश्चिन्न बुद्ध्यते .. 31 ..
5.77.m: Therefore, afflicted by extreme passion, he gazed upon her [body], / leaving aside her face which was veiled with cloth, so that no one might notice.

5.77.s:
na śaṃbhorlajjayā vaktraṃ pratyakṣaṃ sa vyalokayat ..
na ca sā lajjayāviṣṭā karoti prakaṭaṃ mukham .. 32..
5.77.d:
न शंभोर्लज्जया वक्त्रं प्रत्यक्षं स व्यलोकयत् ..
न च सा लज्जयाविष्टा करोति प्रकटं मुखम् .. 32..
5.77.m: Out of shame before Śambhu, he did not look directly at her face; / nor did she, overcome with shame, reveal her face.

5.77.s:
tatastaddarśanārthāya sa upāyaṃ vyalo kayat ..
dhūmadvāreṇa kāmārtaścakāra ca tataḥ param .. 33 ..
5.77.d:
ततस्तद्दर्शनार्थाय स उपायं व्यलो कयत् ..
धूमद्वारेण कामार्तश्चकार च ततः परम् .. 33 ..
5.77.m: Then, in order to behold it, he devised a stratagem; / stricken with passion, he subsequently acted by means of smoke.

5.77.s:
ārdreṃdhanāni bhūrīṇi kṣiptvākṣitvā vibhāvasau ..
svalpājyāhutivinyāsādārdradravyodbhava stathā .. 34 ..
5.77.d:
आर्द्रेंधनानि भूरीणि क्षिप्त्वाक्षित्वा विभावसौ ..
स्वल्पाज्याहुतिविन्यासादार्द्रद्रव्योद्भव स्तथा .. 34 ..
5.77.m: By repeatedly casting copious wet fuel into the fire, / and from offering a meager oblation of clarified butter, [dense smoke] arose from the damp substances.

5.77.s:
etasminnaṃtare dhūmaḥ prādurbhūtaḥ samaṃtataḥ ..
tādṛgyena tamobhūtaṃ vedimūlaṃ vinirmitam .. 35 ..
5.77.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे धूमः प्रादुर्भूतः समंततः ..
तादृग्येन तमोभूतं वेदिमूलं विनिर्मितम् .. 35 ..
5.77.m: In the meantime, smoke burst forth on all sides, / such that the base of the altar was made pitch dark.

5.77.s:
tato dhūmākulenetre bhagavāṃstripu rāntakaḥ ..
hastābhyāṃ chādayāmāsa ye'nye tatra vyavasthitāḥ .. 36 ..
5.77.d:
ततो धूमाकुलेनेत्रे भगवांस्त्रिपु रान्तकः ..
हस्ताभ्यां छादयामास येऽन्ये तत्र व्यवस्थिताः .. 36 ..
5.77.m: Then, their eyes troubled by the smoke, the blessed destroyer of Tripura / and the others who were present there covered [their eyes] with their hands.

5.77.s:
tato vastraṃ samutkṣipya satīvaktraṃ pitāmahaḥ ..
vīkṣayāmāsa kāmārtaḥ prahṛṣṭenāṃtarātmanā .. 37 ..
5.77.d:
ततो वस्त्रं समुत्क्षिप्य सतीवक्त्रं पितामहः ..
वीक्षयामास कामार्तः प्रहृष्टेनांतरात्मना .. 37 ..
5.77.m: Then the grandfather, afflicted with passion, lifted the garment / and gazed upon the face of Satī with an inner soul full of delight.

5.77.s:
tasya retaḥ pracaskanda tatastadvīkṣaṇāddrutam ..
patitaṃ ca dharāpṛṣṭhe tuṣāracayasaṃnibham .. 38
5.77.d:
तस्य रेतः प्रचस्कन्द ततस्तद्वीक्षणाद्द्रुतम् ..
पतितं च धरापृष्ठे तुषारचयसंनिभम् .. 38
5.77.m: Then, from that gaze, his semen immediately flowed forth / and fell upon the surface of the earth, resembling a heap of frost.

5.77.s:
tataśca sikataughenā tatkṣaṇātpadmasaṃbhavaḥ ..
chādayāmāsa tadreto yathā kaścinna buddhyate .. 39 ..
5.77.d:
ततश्च सिकतौघेना तत्क्षणात्पद्मसंभवः ..
छादयामास तद्रेतो यथा कश्चिन्न बुद्ध्यते .. 39 ..
5.77.m: And then, in that moment, the lotus-born [Brahmā] covered that semen / with a heap of sand, so that no one might notice.

5.77.s:
atha tadbhagavāñcchaṃbhurjñātvā divyena cakṣuṣā ..
reto'vaskandanāttasya kopādetaduvāca ha .. 6.77.40 ..
5.77.d:
अथ तद्भगवाञ्च्छंभुर्ज्ञात्वा दिव्येन चक्षुषा ..
रेतोऽवस्कन्दनात्तस्य कोपादेतदुवाच ह .. 6.77.40 ..
5.77.m: Then the blessed Śambhu, knowing that by his divine eye, / spoke this out of anger on account of the shedding of his semen:

5.77.s:
kimetadvihitaṃ pāpa tvayā karma vigarhitam ..
naivārhā mama kāntāyā vaktravīkṣā'nurāgataḥ .. 41 ..
5.77.d:
किमेतद्विहितं पाप त्वया कर्म विगर्हितम् ..
नैवार्हा मम कान्ताया वक्त्रवीक्षाऽनुरागतः .. 41 ..
5.77.m: "O sinner, what is this reprehensible deed that you have committed? / It was entirely improper to look upon my beloved’s face with lust!

5.77.s:
tvaṃ vetsi śaṃkareṇaitatkarmajālaṃ na viṃditam..
trailokye'pi mayā'pyasti gūḍhaṃ tatsyātkathaṃ vidhe..
yatkiñcittriṣu lokeṣu jaṃgamaṃ sthāvaraṃ tathā ..
tasyāhaṃ madhyago mūḍha tailaṃ yadvattilāṃtagam.. 43 ..
5.77.d:
त्वं वेत्सि शंकरेणैतत्कर्मजालं न विंदितम्..
त्रैलोक्येऽपि मयाऽप्यस्ति गूढं तत्स्यात्कथं विधे..
यत्किञ्चित्त्रिषु लोकेषु जंगमं स्थावरं तथा ..
तस्याहं मध्यगो मूढ तैलं यद्वत्तिलांतगम्.. 43 ..
5.77.m: You think this web of deeds was not perceived by Śaṃkara; / yet how could anything in the three worlds remain hidden from me, O creator? / Whatever is moving or unmoving in the three worlds, / I dwell within it, O fool, just like oil within sesame seeds.

5.77.s:
tasmātspṛśa nijaṃ śīrṣaṃ brahmannetadasaṃśayam..
yāvadevaṃ gate brahmā śiraḥ spṛśati pāṇinā ..
tāvattatra sthitaḥ sākṣāttadrūpo vṛṣavāhanaḥ .. 44 ..
5.77.d:
तस्मात्स्पृश निजं शीर्षं ब्रह्मन्नेतदसंशयम्..
यावदेवं गते ब्रह्मा शिरः स्पृशति पाणिना ..
तावत्तत्र स्थितः साक्षात्तद्रूपो वृषवाहनः .. 44 ..
5.77.m: Therefore touch your own head, O Brahmā, without any doubt!" / As Brahmā thus touched his head with his hand, / in that very instant the rider of the bull appeared manifest directly in that form.

5.77.s:
tato lajjāparītāṃgaḥ sthitaścādhomukho dvijāḥ ..
indrādyairamaraiḥ sarvaiḥ sahitaḥ sarvataḥ sthitaiḥ .. 45 ..
5.77.d:
ततो लज्जापरीतांगः स्थितश्चाधोमुखो द्विजाः ..
इन्द्राद्यैरमरैः सर्वैः सहितः सर्वतः स्थितैः .. 45 ..
5.77.m: Then, O twice-born ones, with his limbs filled with shame, he stood with downcast face / in the presence of all the immortals, Indra and the rest, who stood on all sides.

5.77.s:
athā'sau lajjayāviṣṭaḥ praṇipatya maheśvaram ..
provāca ca stutiṃ kṛtvā kṣamyatāṃ kṣamyatāmiti .. 46 ..
5.77.d:
अथाऽसौ लज्जयाविष्टः प्रणिपत्य महेश्वरम् ..
प्रोवाच च स्तुतिं कृत्वा क्षम्यतां क्षम्यतामिति .. 46 ..
5.77.m: Then, overcome with shame, he prostrated himself before Maheśvara, / and having praised him, he said: "Forgive me, forgive me!

5.77.s:
asya pāpasya śuddhyarthaṃ prāya ścittaṃ vada prabho ..
nigrahaṃ ca yathānyāyaṃ yena pāpaṃ prayāti me .. 47 ..
5.77.d:
अस्य पापस्य शुद्ध्यर्थं प्राय श्चित्तं वद प्रभो ..
निग्रहं च यथान्यायं येन पापं प्रयाति मे .. 47 ..
5.77.m: Declare, O Lord, an expiation for the purification of this sin, / and punishment according to justice, so that my sin may depart."

5.77.s:
.. śrībhagavānuvāca.. ..
anenaiva tu rūpeṇa mastakasthena vai tataḥ ..
tapaḥ kuru samādhistho mamārādhanatatparaḥ .. 48 ..
5.77.d:
.. श्रीभगवानुवाच.. ..
अनेनैव तु रूपेण मस्तकस्थेन वै ततः ..
तपः कुरु समाधिस्थो ममाराधनतत्परः .. 48 ..
5.77.m: The Blessed Lord said: / "Indeed, in this very form residing upon your head, / perform austerity, established in absorption, dedicated to worshipping me.

5.77.s:
khyātiṃ yāsyati sarvatra nāmnā rudraśiraḥ kṣitau ..
sādhakaḥ sarvakṛtyānāṃ tejobhājāṃ dvijanma nām .. 49 ..
5.77.d:
ख्यातिं यास्यति सर्वत्र नाम्ना रुद्रशिरः क्षितौ ..
साधकः सर्वकृत्यानां तेजोभाजां द्विजन्म नाम् .. 49 ..
5.77.m: It will attain renown everywhere on earth by the name Rudraśiras, / the fulfiller of all rites for radiant twice-borns.

5.77.s:
mānuṣāṇāmidaṃ kṛtyaṃ yasmāccīrṇaṃ tvayā''dhunā ..
tasmāttvaṃ mānuṣo bhūtvā vicariṣyasi bhūtale . 6.77.50 ..
5.77.d:
मानुषाणामिदं कृत्यं यस्माच्चीर्णं त्वया'ऽधुना ..
तस्मात्त्वं मानुषो भूत्वा विचरिष्यसि भूतले . 6.77.50 ..
5.77.m: Because this deed of mortals was committed by you now, / therefore you shall become a mortal and wander upon the surface of the earth.

5.77.s:
yastvāṃ cānena rūpeṇa dṛṣṭvā pṛcchāṃ kariṣyati ..
kimetadbrahmaṇo mūrdhni bhagavāṃstripurāṃtakaḥ .. 51 ..
5.77.d:
यस्त्वां चानेन रूपेण दृष्ट्वा पृच्छां करिष्यति ..
किमेतद्ब्रह्मणो मूर्ध्नि भगवांस्त्रिपुरांतकः .. 51 ..
5.77.m: Whoever, having seen you in this form, shall ask: / 'What is this blessed destroyer of Tripura doing on Brahmā’s head?'—

5.77.s:
tataste ceṣṭitaṃ sarvaṃ kautukācca śṛṇoti yaḥ ..
paradārakṛtātpāpāttato muktiṃ prayāsyati .. 52 ..
5.77.d:
ततस्ते चेष्टितं सर्वं कौतुकाच्च शृणोति यः ..
परदारकृतात्पापात्ततो मुक्तिं प्रयास्यति .. 52 ..
5.77.m: and then hears your entire conduct out of curiosity, / shall attain liberation from the sin committed regarding another's wife.

5.77.s:
yathāyathā janastvetatkṛtyaṃ te kīrtayiṣyati ..
tathātathā viśuddhiste pāpasyāsya bhaviṣyati .. 53 ..
5.77.d:
यथायथा जनस्त्वेतत्कृत्यं ते कीर्तयिष्यति ..
तथातथा विशुद्धिस्ते पापस्यास्य भविष्यति .. 53 ..
5.77.m: In whatever manner people proclaim this deed of yours, / in that very manner your purification from this sin shall occur.

5.77.s:
etadeva hi te brahmanprāyaścittaṃ prakīrtitam..
janahāsyakaraṃ loke tava garhākaraṃ param .. 54 ..
5.77.d:
एतदेव हि ते ब्रह्मन्प्रायश्चित्तं प्रकीर्तितम्..
जनहास्यकरं लोके तव गर्हाकरं परम् .. 54 ..
5.77.m: For this indeed is proclaimed as your expiation, O Brahmā: / causing ridicule among people in the world, bringing you supreme reproach.

5.77.s:
etacca tava vīryaṃ tu patitaṃ vedimadhyagam ..
kāmārtasya mayā dṛṣṭaṃ naitadvyarthaṃ bhaviṣyati .. 55 ..
5.77.d:
एतच्च तव वीर्यं तु पतितं वेदिमध्यगम् ..
कामार्तस्य मया दृष्टं नैतद्व्यर्थं भविष्यति .. 55 ..
5.77.m: And this semen of yours that fell upon the altar / when you were stricken with passion, seen by me, shall not be in vain.

5.77.s:
yāvanmātraiḥ parispṛṣṭametatsaikatareṇubhiḥ ..
tāvanmātrā bhaviṣyaṃti munayaḥ saṃśitavratāḥ .. 56 ..
5.77.d:
यावन्मात्रैः परिस्पृष्टमेतत्सैकतरेणुभिः ..
तावन्मात्रा भविष्यंति मुनयः संशितव्रताः .. 56 ..
5.77.m: By as many grains of sand as it has been touched, / just so many sages of strict vows shall come into being,

5.77.s:
vālakhilyā iti khyātāḥ sarveṃ'guṣṭhapramāṇakāḥ ..
tapovīryasamopetāḥ śāpānugrahakārakāḥ .. 57 ..
5.77.d:
वालखिल्या इति ख्याताः सर्वेंऽगुष्ठप्रमाणकाः ..
तपोवीर्यसमोपेताः शापानुग्रहकारकाः .. 57 ..
5.77.m: known as the Vālakhilyas, all of them thumb-sized in measure, / endowed with the power of austerity, capable of cursing and bestowing grace."

5.77.s:
etasminnaṃtare tasmādvedimadhyācca tatkṣaṇāt ..
aṣṭāśītisahasrāṇi munīnāṃ bhāvitātmanām ..
aṃguṣṭhakapramāṇāni niṣkrāntāni dvijottamāḥ .. 58 ..
5.77.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे तस्माद्वेदिमध्याच्च तत्क्षणात् ..
अष्टाशीतिसहस्राणि मुनीनां भावितात्मनाम् ..
अंगुष्ठकप्रमाणानि निष्क्रान्तानि द्विजोत्तमाः .. 58 ..
5.77.m: In that interval, from the middle of the altar at that very moment, / eighty-eight thousand sages of cultivated self, / thumb-sized in measure, came forth, O best of the twice-born.

5.77.s:
tataste praṇipatyoccaiḥ procurdevaṃ pitāmaham ..
sthānaṃ darśaya nastāta tapo'rthaṃ kalivarjitam .. 59 ..
5.77.d:
ततस्ते प्रणिपत्योच्चैः प्रोचुर्देवं पितामहम् ..
स्थानं दर्शय नस्तात तपोऽर्थं कलिवर्जितम् .. 59 ..
5.77.m: Then, bowing down, they spoke loudly to god Pitāmaha: / "Show us, O father, a place free of strife for the sake of austerity."

5.77.s:
.. pitāmaha uvāca .. ..
asminkṣetre mayā sārdhaṃ kurudhvaṃ putrakāstapaḥ ..
gamiṣyatha parāṃ siddhiṃ yena loke sudurlabhām .. 6.77.60 ..
5.77.d:
.. पितामह उवाच .. ..
अस्मिन्क्षेत्रे मया सार्धं कुरुध्वं पुत्रकास्तपः ..
गमिष्यथ परां सिद्धिं येन लोके सुदुर्लभाम् .. 6.77.60 ..
5.77.m: Pitāmaha said: / "In this sacred field, perform austerity along with me, O sons, / whereby you shall attain the supreme perfection that is very difficult to attain in the world."

5.77.s:
te tatheti pratijñāya kṛtvā tatrāśramaṃ śubham ..
vālakhilyāstapaścakruḥ saṃsiddhiṃ ca parāṃ gatāḥ .. 61 ..
5.77.d:
ते तथेति प्रतिज्ञाय कृत्वा तत्राश्रमं शुभम् ..
वालखिल्यास्तपश्चक्रुः संसिद्धिं च परां गताः .. 61 ..
5.77.m: Agreeing with 'So be it,' and having built an auspicious hermitage there, / the Vālakhilyas performed austerity and attained supreme perfection.

5.77.s:
atha brahmāpi tatkarma sarvaṃ vaivāhikaṃ kramāt ..
samāptimanayatproktaṃ yacchrutau tena ca svayam .. 62 ..
5.77.d:
अथ ब्रह्मापि तत्कर्म सर्वं वैवाहिकं क्रमात् ..
समाप्तिमनयत्प्रोक्तं यच्छ्रुतौ तेन च स्वयम् .. 62 ..
5.77.m: Then Brahmā also brought that entire nuptial rite in due order / to completion, as was prescribed in the Veda by himself.

5.77.s:
patatsu puṣpavarṣeṣu samantādgaganāṃgaṇāt ..
vādyamāneṣu vādyeṣu gīya mānaiścagītakaiḥ .. 63 ..
5.77.d:
पतत्सु पुष्पवर्षेषु समन्ताद्गगनांगणात् ..
वाद्यमानेषु वाद्येषु गीय मानैश्चगीतकैः .. 63 ..
5.77.m: While showers of flowers fell on all sides from the courtyard of the sky, / while musical instruments were played, and songs were being sung,

5.77.s:
paṭhatsu vipramukhyeṣu nṛtyamānāsu rāgataḥ ..
raṃbhādiṣu purandhrīṣu devānāṃ dṛṅmanoharam.. 64 ..
5.77.d:
पठत्सु विप्रमुख्येषु नृत्यमानासु रागतः ..
रंभादिषु पुरन्ध्रीषु देवानां दृङ्मनोहरम्.. 64 ..
5.77.m: while the foremost brahmins recited, and married women [of heaven] such as Rambhā / danced passionately, captivating to the eyes of the gods—

5.77.s:
evaṃ mahotsavo jajñe tata stuṃburupūrvakaiḥ ..
gīyamāneṣu gīteṣu yathāpūrvaṃ triviṣṭape .. 65 ..
5.77.d:
एवं महोत्सवो जज्ञे तत स्तुंबुरुपूर्वकैः ..
गीयमानेषु गीतेषु यथापूर्वं त्रिविष्टपे .. 65 ..
5.77.m: thus a great festival took place, as songs led by Tumburu / were sung as formerly in heaven.

5.77.s:
atha karmāvasāne sa bhagavāṃstripurāṃtakaḥ ..
provāca padmajaṃ bhaktyā dakṣiṇāṃ te dadāmi kim .. 66 ..
5.77.d:
अथ कर्मावसाने स भगवांस्त्रिपुरांतकः ..
प्रोवाच पद्मजं भक्त्या दक्षिणां ते ददामि किम् .. 66 ..
5.77.m: Then, at the conclusion of the rite, the blessed destroyer of Tripura / said to the lotus-born [Brahmā] with devotion: "What sacrificial fee may I give you,

5.77.s:
vaivāhikī suraśreṣṭha yadyapi syātsudurlabhā ..
brūhi śīghraṃ mahābhāga nādeyaṃ vidyate mama .. 67 ..
5.77.d:
वैवाहिकी सुरश्रेष्ठ यद्यपि स्यात्सुदुर्लभा ..
ब्रूहि शीघ्रं महाभाग नादेयं विद्यते मम .. 67 ..
5.77.m: pertaining to marriage, O best of the gods, even if it be very difficult to obtain? / Speak quickly, O fortunate one; there is nothing that I cannot give."

5.77.s:
.. pitāmaha uvāca .. ..
anenaiva tu rūpeṇa vedyāmasyāṃ sureśvara ..
tvayā stheyaṃ sadaivātra nṛṇāṃ pāpaviśuddhaye .. 68 ..
5.77.d:
.. पितामह उवाच .. ..
अनेनैव तु रूपेण वेद्यामस्यां सुरेश्वर ..
त्वया स्थेयं सदैवात्र नृणां पापविशुद्धये .. 68 ..
5.77.m: Pitāmaha said: / "O Lord of gods, in this very form upon this altar / you must reside always here for the purification of men's sins,

5.77.s:
yena te sannidhau kṛtvā svāśramaṃ śaśiśekhara ..
tapaḥ karomi nāśāya pāpasyāsya mahattamam .. 69 ..
5.77.d:
येन ते सन्निधौ कृत्वा स्वाश्रमं शशिशेखर ..
तपः करोमि नाशाय पापस्यास्य महत्तमम् .. 69 ..
5.77.m: so that, having made my hermitage in your presence, O moon-crested one, / I may perform the highest austerity for the destruction of this sin.

5.77.s:
caitraśuklatrayodaśyāṃ nakṣatre bhagadaivate ..
sūryavāreṇa yo bhaktyā vīkṣayiṣyati mānavaḥ ..
tadaiva tasya pāpāni prayāsyanti ca saṃkṣayam .. 6.77.70 ..
5.77.d:
चैत्रशुक्लत्रयोदश्यां नक्षत्रे भगदैवते ..
सूर्यवारेण यो भक्त्या वीक्षयिष्यति मानवः ..
तदैव तस्य पापानि प्रयास्यन्ति च संक्षयम् .. 6.77.70 ..
5.77.m: On the thirteenth day of the bright fortnight of Caitra, under the lunar mansion of Bhaga, / on a Sunday, whatever mortal beholds [you] with devotion, / right then their sins shall go to destruction.

5.77.s:
yā nārī durbhagā vandhyā kāṇā rūpavivarjitā ..
sā'pi tvaddarśanādeva bhaviṣyati surūpadhṛk ..
prajāvatī subhogāḍhyā subhagā nātra saṃśayaḥ .. 71 ..
5.77.d:
या नारी दुर्भगा वन्ध्या काणा रूपविवर्जिता ..
साऽपि त्वद्दर्शनादेव भविष्यति सुरूपधृक् ..
प्रजावती सुभोगाढ्या सुभगा नात्र संशयः .. 71 ..
5.77.m: Whatever woman is unfortunate, barren, one-eyed, or bereft of beauty, / even she, merely by darśana of you, shall become endowed with exquisite form, / having offspring, rich in good fortunes, and blessed; of this there is no doubt."

5.77.s:
.. maheśvara uvāca .. ..
hitāya sarvalokānāṃ vedyāmasyāṃ vyavasthitaḥ ..
sthāsyāmi sahitaḥ patnyā satyātva dvacanādvidhe .. 72 ..
5.77.d:
.. महेश्वर उवाच .. ..
हिताय सर्वलोकानां वेद्यामस्यां व्यवस्थितः ..
स्थास्यामि सहितः पत्न्या सत्यात्व द्वचनाद्विधे .. 72 ..
5.77.m: Maheśvara said: / For the welfare of all the worlds, stationed on this altar, / I shall remain together with my wife, O Brahmā, in truth, because of your word. (72)

5.77.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
evaṃ sa bhagavāṃstatra sabhāryo vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ ..
vidyate vedimadhyastho lokānāṃ pāpanāśanaḥ 0.. 73 ..
5.77.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
एवं स भगवांस्तत्र सभार्यो वृषभध्वजः ..
विद्यते वेदिमध्यस्थो लोकानां पापनाशनः 0.. 73 ..
5.77.m: Sūta said: / Thus the Blessed One, whose banner bears the bull, together with his wife, / remains standing in the midst of the altar, destroying the sins of the worlds. (73)

5.77.s:
etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ yathā tasya purā'bhavat ..
vivāho vṛṣanāthasya manau svāyaṃbhuve dvijāḥ .. 74 ..
5.77.d:
एतद्वः सर्वमाख्यातं यथा तस्य पुराऽभवत् ..
विवाहो वृषनाथस्य मनौ स्वायंभुवे द्विजाः .. 74 ..
5.77.m: All this has been related to you, how formerly his marriage, / the marriage of the Lord whose emblem is the bull, took place in the Svāyambhuva Manvantara, O twice-born ones. (74)

5.77.s:
vivāhasamaye prāpte prārambhe vā śṛṇoti yaḥ ..
etadākhyānamavyagraṃ saṃpūjya vṛṣabhadhvajam ..
tasyā'vighnaṃ bhavetsarvaṃ karma vaivāhikaṃ ca yat .. 79 ..
kanyā ca sukhasaubhāgya śīlācāraguṇānvitā ..
tathā syātputriṇī sādhvī pativrataparāyaṇā .. 76 ..
iti śrīskāṃde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ sahitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṃḍe śrīhāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye harāśrayavedikāmāhātmyavarṇanaṃnāma saptasaptatitamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 77 .. .. dha ..
5.77.d:
विवाहसमये प्राप्ते प्रारम्भे वा शृणोति यः ..
एतदाख्यानमव्यग्रं संपूज्य वृषभध्वजम् ..
तस्याऽविघ्नं भवेत्सर्वं कर्म वैवाहिकं च यत् .. 79 ..
कन्या च सुखसौभाग्य शीलाचारगुणान्विता ..
तथा स्यात्पुत्रिणी साध्वी पतिव्रतपरायणा .. 76 ..
इति श्रीस्कांदे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां सहितायां षष्ठे नागरखंडे श्रीहाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये हराश्रयवेदिकामाहात्म्यवर्णनंनाम सप्तसप्ततितमोऽध्यायः .. 77 .. .. ध ..
5.77.m:
Whenever a wedding arrives or at its beginning, whoever listens / with focused mind to this narrative after having worshipped the one whose banner bears the bull, / every rite of his connected with the wedding will be free of obstacles; (75)
and the maiden will be endowed with happiness, good fortune, good character, proper conduct, and virtues; / likewise, she will have sons, be virtuous, and devoted to her husband. (76)
Thus ends the seventy-seventh chapter, named 'Description of the Glory of the Altar Serving as the Abode of Hara', in the Glory of the Sacred Field of Śrī Hāṭakeśvara, in the Nāgarakhaṇḍa, the sixth [part] in the Śrī Skanda Mahāpurāṇa consisting of eighty-one thousand verses. (77)

5.78.s:
.. ṛṣaya ūcuḥ .. ..
brahmaṇā katame sthāne tatra sūta kṛtaṃ tapaḥ ..
vālakhilyaiśca taiḥ sarvairmunibhiḥ śaṃsitavrataiḥ .. 1 ..
5.78.d:
.. ऋषय ऊचुः .. ..
ब्रह्मणा कतमे स्थाने तत्र सूत कृतं तपः ..
वालखिल्यैश्च तैः सर्वैर्मुनिभिः शंसितव्रतैः .. 1 ..
5.78.m: The seers said: / In what place there, O Sūta, was austerity performed by Brahmā, / and by all those Vālakhilyas, sages celebrated for their vows? (1)

5.78.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
tasyā vāyavyadigbhāge haravedyā dvijottamāḥ ..
samyakchraddhāprayatnena brahmaṇā vihitaṃ tapaḥ .. 2 ..
5.78.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
तस्या वायव्यदिग्भागे हरवेद्या द्विजोत्तमाः ..
सम्यक्छ्रद्धाप्रयत्नेन ब्रह्मणा विहितं तपः .. 2 ..
5.78.m: Sūta said: / In the north-western quarter of that altar of Hara, O best of the twice-born, / austerity was performed by Brahmā with proper faith and diligence, (2)

5.78.s:
paścime vālakhilyaiśca japasnānaparāyaṇaiḥ ..
tatrāścaryamabhūdyadvai pūrvaṃ brāhmaṇa sattamāḥ ..
āśrame caturāsyasya tadvo vakṣyāmi sāṃpratam .. 3 ..
5.78.d:
पश्चिमे वालखिल्यैश्च जपस्नानपरायणैः ..
तत्राश्चर्यमभूद्यद्वै पूर्वं ब्राह्मण सत्तमाः ..
आश्रमे चतुरास्यस्य तद्वो वक्ष्यामि सांप्रतम् .. 3 ..
5.78.m: and in the west by the Vālakhilyas devoted to recitation and ritual ablution. / What wonderful thing indeed took place there formerly, O best of brahmins, / in the hermitage of the four-faced one, that I shall now tell you. (3)

5.78.s:
tatra duścāriṇī kācidrātrau brāhmaṇavaṃśajā ..
devadattaṃ samāsādya vallabhaṃ ramate sadā .. .. 4 ..
5.78.d:
तत्र दुश्चारिणी काचिद्रात्रौ ब्राह्मणवंशजा ..
देवदत्तं समासाद्य वल्लभं रमते सदा .. .. 4 ..
5.78.m: There, a certain unchaste woman born of a brahmin lineage, / having met her lover Devadatta, would constantly take pleasure at night. (4)

5.78.s:
ajñātā patinā mātrā tathānyairapi bāṃdhavaiḥ ..
kṛṣṇapakṣaṃ samāsādya vijane hṛṣṭamānasā .. 5 ..
5.78.d:
अज्ञाता पतिना मात्रा तथान्यैरपि बांधवैः ..
कृष्णपक्षं समासाद्य विजने हृष्टमानसा .. 5 ..
5.78.m: Unnoticed by her husband, by her mother, and also by other relatives, / taking advantage of the dark fortnight, she was delighted at heart in a solitary place. (5)

5.78.s:
kasyacittvatha kālasya dṛṣṭā sā kenaci ddvijāḥ ..
tatrasthā jārasaṃyuktā svabhartuśca niveditā .. 6 ..
5.78.d:
कस्यचित्त्वथ कालस्य दृष्टा सा केनचि द्द्विजाः ..
तत्रस्था जारसंयुक्ता स्वभर्तुश्च निवेदिता .. 6 ..
5.78.m: Then, after some time, she was seen by someone, O twice-born ones, / staying there united with her paramour, and she was reported to her husband. (6)

5.78.s:
athāsau kopasaṃyuktastasyā bhartā suniṣṭhuraiḥ ..
vākyaistāṃ garhayāmāsa prahāraiścāpya tāḍayat .. 7 ..
5.78.d:
अथासौ कोपसंयुक्तस्तस्या भर्ता सुनिष्ठुरैः ..
वाक्यैस्तां गर्हयामास प्रहारैश्चाप्य ताडयत् .. 7 ..
5.78.m: Then her husband, filled with wrath, reviled her with very harsh words / and struck her with blows. (7)

5.78.s:
atha sā dhārṣṭyamāsādya strīsvabhāvaṃ samāśritā ..
provāca bāṣpapūrṇākṣī dīnāṃjalipuṭā sthitā .. 8 ..
5.78.d:
अथ सा धार्ष्ट्यमासाद्य स्त्रीस्वभावं समाश्रिता ..
प्रोवाच बाष्पपूर्णाक्षी दीनांजलिपुटा स्थिता .. 8 ..
5.78.m: Then she, having resorted to boldness according to womanly nature, / spoke with her eyes filled with tears, standing with her hands joined piteously: (8)

5.78.s:
kiṃ māṃ durjanavākyena tvaṃ tāḍayasi niṣṭhuraiḥ ..
prahārairdoṣanirmuktāṃ tvatpādapraṇatāṃ vibho .. 9 ..
5.78.d:
किं मां दुर्जनवाक्येन त्वं ताडयसि निष्ठुरैः ..
प्रहारैर्दोषनिर्मुक्तां त्वत्पादप्रणतां विभो .. 9 ..
5.78.m: “Why do you strike me with harsh blows on the word of a wicked person, / [me] who am free from fault, bowed down at your feet, O lord? (9)

5.78.s:
ahaṃ tvāṃ śapathaṃ kṛtvā bhakṣayitvā'tha vā viṣam ..
praviśya havyavāhaṃ vā kariṣye pratyayānvitam.. 6.78.10 ..
5.78.d:
अहं त्वां शपथं कृत्वा भक्षयित्वाऽथ वा विषम् ..
प्रविश्य हव्यवाहं वा करिष्ये प्रत्ययान्वितम्.. 6.78.10 ..
5.78.m: I will make you confident by taking an oath, or by consuming poison, / or by entering the carrier of oblations.” (10)

5.78.s:
atha tāṃ brāhmaṇaḥ prāha yadi tvaṃ pāpavarjitā ..
purato devaviprāṇāṃ kuru divyagrahaṃ svayam.. 11 ..
5.78.d:
अथ तां ब्राह्मणः प्राह यदि त्वं पापवर्जिता ..
पुरतो देवविप्राणां कुरु दिव्यग्रहं स्वयम्.. 11 ..
5.78.m: Then the brahmin said to her: “If you are free from sin, / yourself undergo an ordeal in the presence of the gods and the brahmins.” (11)

5.78.s:
sā tatheti pratijñāya sāhasena samanvitā ..
divyagrahaṃ tataścakre yathoktavidhinā satī .. 12 ..
5.78.d:
सा तथेति प्रतिज्ञाय साहसेन समन्विता ..
दिव्यग्रहं ततश्चक्रे यथोक्तविधिना सती .. 12 ..
5.78.m: Agreeing with “So be it”, she, endowed with audacity, / then underwent the ordeal in accordance with the prescribed rule, seemingly virtuous. (12)

5.78.s:
śuddhiṃ ca prāptā sarveṣāṃ bandhūnāṃ ca dvijanmanām ..
purataśca gurūṇāṃ ca devānāmapi pāpakṛt .. 13 ..
5.78.d:
शुद्धिं च प्राप्ता सर्वेषां बन्धूनां च द्विजन्मनाम् ..
पुरतश्च गुरूणां च देवानामपि पापकृत् .. 13 ..
5.78.m: And the evil-doer attained purification in front of all her relatives, the twice-born, / her elders, and even the gods. (13)

5.78.s:
etasminnantare tasyāḥ sādhuvādo mahānabhūt ..
dhikchabdaśca tathā patyuḥ sarvairdattaḥ sugarhitaḥ .. 14 ..
5.78.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे तस्याः साधुवादो महानभूत् ..
धिक्छब्दश्च तथा पत्युः सर्वैर्दत्तः सुगर्हितः .. 14 ..
5.78.m: At that moment, great applause arose for her, / and a cry of 'Fie!' was given by all in harsh censure to the husband: (14)

5.78.s:
aho pāpasamācāro duṣṭo'yaṃ brāhmaṇādhamaḥ ..
apāpāṃ dharmapatnīṃ yo mithyādoṣeṇayojayet .. 15 ..
5.78.d:
अहो पापसमाचारो दुष्टोऽयं ब्राह्मणाधमः ..
अपापां धर्मपत्नीं यो मिथ्यादोषेणयोजयेत् .. 15 ..
5.78.m: “Oh, wicked is the conduct of this vile, wretched brahmin, / who falsely accuses his sinless lawful wife of fault!” (15)

5.78.s:
evaṃ sa nindyamānastu sarvalokairdvijottamāḥ ..
kopaṃ cakre tato vahniṃ samuddiśya saduḥkhitaḥ .. 16 ..
5.78.d:
एवं स निन्द्यमानस्तु सर्वलोकैर्द्विजोत्तमाः ..
कोपं चक्रे ततो वह्निं समुद्दिश्य सदुःखितः .. 16 ..
5.78.m: Thus being reproached by all the people, O best of the twice-born, / he then, greatly distressed, directed his anger toward the Fire. (16)

5.78.s:
śāpaṃ dātuṃ matiṃ cakre tato vahneḥ suduḥkhitaḥ ..
abravītparuṣaṃ vākyaṃ nindamānaḥ punaḥpunaḥ .. .. 17 ..
5.78.d:
शापं दातुं मतिं चक्रे ततो वह्नेः सुदुःखितः ..
अब्रवीत्परुषं वाक्यं निन्दमानः पुनःपुनः .. .. 17 ..
5.78.m: Greatly distressed, he then set his mind on giving a curse to the Fire; / reviling him again and again, he spoke harsh words: (17)

5.78.s:
mayā svayaṃ pradṛṣṭeyaṃ jāreṇa saha saṃgatā ..
tvayā vahne supāpeyaṃ na kasmādbhasmasātkṛtā .. 18 ..
5.78.d:
मया स्वयं प्रदृष्टेयं जारेण सह संगता ..
त्वया वह्ने सुपापेयं न कस्माद्भस्मसात्कृता .. 18 ..
5.78.m: “She was directly seen by me myself united with her paramour; / why, O Fire, was this deeply sinful woman not reduced to ashes by you? (18)

5.78.s:
tasmāttvāṃ pāpakarmāṇamasatyapakṣapātinam ..
asaṃdigdhaṃ śapiṣyāmi raudraśāpena sāṃpratam .. 19 ..
5.78.d:
तस्मात्त्वां पापकर्माणमसत्यपक्षपातिनम् ..
असंदिग्धं शपिष्यामि रौद्रशापेन सांप्रतम् .. 19 ..
5.78.m: Therefore, you evil-doer, who take the side of untruth, / I will undoubtedly curse now with a terrible curse.” (19)

5.78.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
tasya tadvacanaṃ śrutvā saṃkruddhasya dvijanmanaḥ ..
saptārcirbhayasaṃtrastaḥ kṛtāṃjaliruvāca tam .. 6.78.20 ..
5.78.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
तस्य तद्वचनं श्रुत्वा संक्रुद्धस्य द्विजन्मनः ..
सप्तार्चिर्भयसंत्रस्तः कृतांजलिरुवाच तम् .. 6.78.20 ..
5.78.m: Sūta said: / Hearing those words of that enraged twice-born man, / the Seven-Flamed One, terrified with fear, said to him with folded hands: (20)

5.78.s:
.. agniruvāca .. ..
naiṣa doṣo mama brahmanyanna dagdhā tava priyā ..
kṛtāgasā'pi me vākyaṃ śṛṇuṣvātra sphuṭeritam .. 21 ..
5.78.d:
.. अग्निरुवाच .. ..
नैष दोषो मम ब्रह्मन्यन्न दग्धा तव प्रिया ..
कृतागसाऽपि मे वाक्यं शृणुष्वात्र स्फुटेरितम् .. 21 ..
5.78.m: Agni said: / “This is not my fault, O brahmin, that your beloved was not burned; / even though she committed an offense, listen to my word clearly spoken in this matter. (21)

5.78.s:
anayā parakāṃtena kṛtaḥ saha samāgamaḥ ..
ciraṃ kālaṃ dvija śreṣṭha tvayā jñātādya vāsare .. 22 ..
5.78.d:
अनया परकांतेन कृतः सह समागमः ..
चिरं कालं द्विज श्रेष्ठ त्वया ज्ञाताद्य वासरे .. 22 ..
5.78.m: Union with another lover was made by her / for a long time, O best of the twice-born; it was known by you only today. (22)

5.78.s:
paraṃ yasmādviśuddhaiṣā mayā dagdhā na sā dvija ..
kāraṇaṃ tacca te vacmi śṛṇuṣvaikamanāḥ sthitaḥ .. 23 ..
5.78.d:
परं यस्माद्विशुद्धैषा मया दग्धा न सा द्विज ..
कारणं तच्च ते वच्मि शृणुष्वैकमनाः स्थितः .. 23 ..
5.78.m: Yet because she was purified, she was not burned by me, O twice-born one; / and the reason for that I tell you: listen with an attentive mind. (23)

5.78.s:
yatrānayā kṛtaḥ saṃgaḥ parakāṃtena vai dvija ..
tasminnāyatane brahmā rudraśīrṣo vyavasthitaḥ .. 24 ..
5.78.d:
यत्रानया कृतः संगः परकांतेन वै द्विज ..
तस्मिन्नायतने ब्रह्मा रुद्रशीर्षो व्यवस्थितः .. 24 ..
5.78.m: Where union was made by her with another lover, O twice-born one, / in that sanctuary Brahmā is situated having the head of Rudra. (24)

5.78.s:
tatra kṛtvā rataṃ citraṃ parakāṃtasamaṃ tadā ..
paśyati sma tato rudraṃ brahmamastakasaṃsthitam .. 25 ..
5.78.d:
तत्र कृत्वा रतं चित्रं परकांतसमं तदा ..
पश्यति स्म ततो रुद्रं ब्रह्ममस्तकसंस्थितम् .. 25 ..
5.78.m: Having engaged in extraordinary lovemaking there with another lover at that time, / she then beheld Rudra situated on the head of Brahmā. (25)

5.78.s:
tataḥ prakṣālayatyaṃgaṃ kuṇḍe tatrāgrataḥ sthite ..
kṛtapāpāpi tenaiṣā śuddhiṃ yāti śucismitā .. .. 26 ..
5.78.d:
ततः प्रक्षालयत्यंगं कुण्डे तत्राग्रतः स्थिते ..
कृतपापापि तेनैषा शुद्धिं याति शुचिस्मिता .. .. 26 ..
5.78.m: Then she washes her body in the pool situated right in front of it; / though having committed sin, she of radiant smile attains purity by that. (26)

5.78.s:
atra pūrvaṃ vipāpmā'bhūdbrahmā lokapitāmahaḥ ..
satīvaktraṃ samālokya kāmārto'pi sa pāpakṛt .. 27 ..
5.78.d:
अत्र पूर्वं विपाप्माऽभूद्ब्रह्मा लोकपितामहः ..
सतीवक्त्रं समालोक्य कामार्तोऽपि स पापकृत् .. 27 ..
5.78.m: Here formerly Brahmā, the grandfather of the worlds, became free from sin, / even though having committed sin, afflicted with passion upon beholding the face of Satī. (27)

5.78.s:
tasmānnāstyatra me doṣaḥ svalpo'pi dvijasattama..
rudraśīrṣaprabhāvo'yaṃ tasya kuṇḍodakasya ca .. 28 ..
5.78.d:
तस्मान्नास्त्यत्र मे दोषः स्वल्पोऽपि द्विजसत्तम..
रुद्रशीर्षप्रभावोऽयं तस्य कुण्डोदकस्य च .. 28 ..
5.78.m: Therefore there is not even the slightest fault on my part in this, O best of the twice-born; / this is the power of the head of Rudra and of the water of that pool. (28)

5.78.s:
tasmādenāṃ samādāya saṃśuddhāṃ pāpavarjitām ..
gṛhaṃ gaccha dvijaśreṣṭha satyametanmayo ditam.. 29 ..
5.78.d:
तस्मादेनां समादाय संशुद्धां पापवर्जिताम् ..
गृहं गच्छ द्विजश्रेष्ठ सत्यमेतन्मयो दितम्.. 29 ..
5.78.m: Therefore, taking this [wife] completely purified and free from sin, / go home, O best of the twice-born; this is the truth spoken by me.” (29)

5.78.s:
.. brāhmaṇa uvāca .. ..
yā mayā sahasā dṛṣṭā svayameva hutāśana ..
parakāṃtena tāṃ nādya śuddhāmapi gṛhaṃ naye .. 6.78.30 ..
5.78.d:
.. ब्राह्मण उवाच .. ..
या मया सहसा दृष्टा स्वयमेव हुताशन ..
परकांतेन तां नाद्य शुद्धामपि गृहं नये .. 6.78.30 ..
5.78.m: The brahmin said: / “She who was seen by myself suddenly, O consumer of oblations, / with another lover, I will not take home today, even if she is purified.” (30)

5.78.s:
ityuktvā ca dvijaśreṣṭhastāṃ tyaktvāpi śucivrataḥ ..
jagāma svagṛhaṃ paścāttathā jagmurjanā gṛhān .. 31 ..
5.78.d:
इत्युक्त्वा च द्विजश्रेष्ठस्तां त्यक्त्वापि शुचिव्रतः ..
जगाम स्वगृहं पश्चात्तथा जग्मुर्जना गृहान् .. 31 ..
5.78.m: Having said this, that best of the twice-born, of pure vows, abandoning her, / went to his own home; afterwards, the people also went to their homes. (31)

5.78.s:
sāpi tena parityaktā patinā hṛṣṭamānasā ..
jñātvā tattīrthamāhātmyaṃ vaiśvānaramukheritam .. 32 ..
5.78.d:
सापि तेन परित्यक्ता पतिना हृष्टमानसा ..
ज्ञात्वा तत्तीर्थमाहात्म्यं वैश्वानरमुखेरितम् .. 32 ..
5.78.m: She too, abandoned by that husband, delighted at heart, / having learned the greatness of that sacred ford spoken from the mouth of Vaiśvānara, (32)

5.78.s:
tenaiva parakāṃtena viśeṣeṇa ratikriyām ..
tasminnāyatane cakre kuṇḍe toyāvagāhanam .. 33 ..
5.78.d:
तेनैव परकांतेन विशेषेण रतिक्रियाम् ..
तस्मिन्नायतने चक्रे कुण्डे तोयावगाहनम् .. 33 ..
5.78.m: engaged all the more in the act of lovemaking with that very paramour / in that sanctuary, and bathed in the water of the pool. (33)

5.78.s:
athānye paralokasya bhītyā'tīva vyavasthitāḥ ..
vimukhāḥ paradāreṣu nāryaścāpi pativratāḥ .. 34 ..
5.78.d:
अथान्ये परलोकस्य भीत्याऽतीव व्यवस्थिताः ..
विमुखाः परदारेषु नार्यश्चापि पतिव्रताः .. 34 ..
5.78.m: Then others, strictly abiding [in virtue] out of great fear of the next world, / turned away from other men's wives, and women likewise were devoted to their husbands. (34)

5.78.s:
dūrato'pi samabhyetya te sarve tatra maṃdire ..
rudraśīrṣābhidhānaṃ ca pracakruḥ suratotsavam .. 35 ..
5.78.d:
दूरतोऽपि समभ्येत्य ते सर्वे तत्र मंदिरे ..
रुद्रशीर्षाभिधानं च प्रचक्रुः सुरतोत्सवम् .. 35 ..
5.78.m: Coming together even from afar, they all engaged in sexual pleasure in that temple, / which bore the name Rudraśīrṣa.

5.78.s:
nimajjaṃti tataḥ kuṇḍe tasminpātakanāśane ..
bhavaṃti pāpanirmuktā rudraśīrṣāvalokanāt .. 36 ..
5.78.d:
निमज्जंति ततः कुण्डे तस्मिन्पातकनाशने ..
भवंति पापनिर्मुक्ता रुद्रशीर्षावलोकनात् .. 36 ..
5.78.m: Then they would bathe in that pond that destroys sins; / they became freed from sin through the darśana of Rudraśīrṣa.

5.78.s:
etasminnaṃtare naṣṭo dharmaḥ patnīsamudbhavaḥ ..
puruṣāṇāṃ tataḥ strīṇāṃ nijakāṃtāsamudbhavaḥ .. 37 ..
5.78.d:
एतस्मिन्नंतरे नष्टो धर्मः पत्नीसमुद्भवः ..
पुरुषाणां ततः स्त्रीणां निजकांतासमुद्भवः .. 37 ..
5.78.m: Meanwhile, the dharma born of marriage was lost / among men, and so among women was the [dharma] born of their own husbands.

5.78.s:
yo yāṃ paśyati rūpāḍhyāṃ nārīmapi kulodbhavām ..
sa tatrānīya saṃhṛṣṭo bhajate dvijasattamāḥ .. 38 ..
5.78.d:
यो यां पश्यति रूपाढ्यां नारीमपि कुलोद्भवाम् ..
स तत्रानीय संहृष्टो भजते द्विजसत्तमाः .. 38 ..
5.78.m: Whatever beautiful woman one saw, even if born of a noble family, / bringing her there, O best of brahmins, he enjoyed her with delight.

5.78.s:
tathā nārī surūpāḍhyaṃ yaṃ paśyati naraṃ kvacit ..
sāpi tatra samānīya kurute suratotsavam .. 39 ..
5.78.d:
तथा नारी सुरूपाढ्यं यं पश्यति नरं क्वचित् ..
सापि तत्र समानीय कुरुते सुरतोत्सवम् .. 39 ..
5.78.m: Likewise, whatever very handsome man a woman saw anywhere, / she too, bringing him there, engaged in sexual pleasure.

5.78.s:
lipyate na ca pāpena kathaṃcittakṛtena ca ..
naro vā yadi vā nārī tattīrthasya prabhāvataḥ .. 6.78.40 ..
5.78.d:
लिप्यते न च पापेन कथंचित्तकृतेन च ..
नरो वा यदि वा नारी तत्तीर्थस्य प्रभावतः .. 6.78.40 ..
5.78.m: And neither a man nor a woman was smeared with the sin committed by that / in any way, by the power of that tīrtha.

5.78.s:
kasyacittvatha kālasya tatra rājā vidūrathaḥ ..
ānarttaviṣaye jajñe vārdhakyaṃ ca kramādyayau .. 41 ..
5.78.d:
कस्यचित्त्वथ कालस्य तत्र राजा विदूरथः ..
आनर्त्तविषये जज्ञे वार्धक्यं च क्रमाद्ययौ .. 41 ..
5.78.m: Then at a certain time there was born a king named Vidūratha / in the territory of Ānarta, and in due course he grew old.

5.78.s:
tasya bhāryā'bhavattanvī taruṇī vararūpadhṛk ..
paścime vayasi prāpte prāṇebhyo'pi garīyasī .. .. 42 ..
5.78.d:
तस्य भार्याऽभवत्तन्वी तरुणी वररूपधृक् ..
पश्चिमे वयसि प्राप्ते प्राणेभ्योऽपि गरीयसी .. .. 42 ..
5.78.m: His wife was slender, youthful, endowed with exquisite beauty, / dearer to him than his own life, when he had reached his advanced age.

5.78.s:
na tasyāḥ sa jarāgrastaścitte vasati pārthivaḥ ..
tasmiṃstīrthe samāgatya vāṃchitaṃ ramate naraḥ .. 43 ..
5.78.d:
न तस्याः स जराग्रस्तश्चित्ते वसति पार्थिवः ..
तस्मिंस्तीर्थे समागत्य वांछितं रमते नरः .. 43 ..
5.78.m: That king, seized by old age, did not abide in her heart; / coming to that tīrtha, a man enjoyed the beloved woman.

5.78.s:
pārthivo'pi parijñāya tasyāstacca viceṣṭitam ..
kopāviṣṭastato gatvā tasminkṣetre suśobhane .. 44 ..
5.78.d:
पार्थिवोऽपि परिज्ञाय तस्यास्तच्च विचेष्टितम् ..
कोपाविष्टस्ततो गत्वा तस्मिन्क्षेत्रे सुशोभने .. 44 ..
5.78.m: The king too, learning of that behavior of hers, / filled with rage, then went to that auspicious sacred field.

5.78.s:
tatkuṇḍaṃ pūrayāmāsa tataḥ pāṃśūtkarairdrutam ..
babhaṃja taṃ ca prāsādaṃ tataḥ provāca dāruṇam .. 45 ..
5.78.d:
तत्कुण्डं पूरयामास ततः पांशूत्करैर्द्रुतम् ..
बभंज तं च प्रासादं ततः प्रोवाच दारुणम् .. 45 ..
5.78.m: He quickly filled up that pond with heaps of dust, / and smashed that temple; then he uttered a terrible [curse]:

5.78.s:
yaścaitatpūritaṃ kuṇḍaṃ pāṃśunā nikhaniṣyati ..
prāsādaṃ ca punaścainaṃ kariṣyati punarnavam .. 46 ..
5.78.d:
यश्चैतत्पूरितं कुण्डं पांशुना निखनिष्यति ..
प्रासादं च पुनश्चैनं करिष्यति पुनर्नवम् .. 46 ..
5.78.m: “Whoever digs out this pond that has been filled with dust / and makes this temple new again,

5.78.s:
paradārakṛtaṃ pāpaṃ tasya saṃpatsyate'khilam ..
yadatra prakariṣyaṃti mānavāḥ kāmamohitāḥ ..47..
5.78.d:
परदारकृतं पापं तस्य संपत्स्यतेऽखिलम् ..
यदत्र प्रकरिष्यंति मानवाः काममोहिताः ..47..
5.78.m: to him shall accrue all the sin committed with another's wife / that men delusion-struck by lust shall commit here.”

5.78.s:
.. sūta uvāca .. ..
evaṃ sa pārthivaḥ procya tāmādāya tataḥ priyām ..
jagāma svagṛhaṃ paścātprahṛṣṭenāṃtarātmanā ..48..
5.78.d:
.. सूत उवाच .. ..
एवं स पार्थिवः प्रोच्य तामादाय ततः प्रियाम् ..
जगाम स्वगृहं पश्चात्प्रहृष्टेनांतरात्मना ..48..
5.78.m: Sūta said: / Having spoken thus, that king, taking that beloved woman, / then went to his own house with a delighted mind.

5.78.s:
atha tāṃ viratāṃ jñātvā so'nyacittāṃ priyāṃ nṛpaḥ ..
yatnena rakṣayāmāsa viśvāsaṃ naiva gacchati .. 49 ..
5.78.d:
अथ तां विरतां ज्ञात्वा सोऽन्यचित्तां प्रियां नृपः ..
यत्नेन रक्षयामास विश्वासं नैव गच्छति .. 49 ..
5.78.m: Then, knowing that beloved wife to be detached and her mind elsewhere, the king / guarded her with effort; he placed no trust [in her] at all.

5.78.s:
anyasmindivase śastraṃ sūkṣmaṃ veṇyāṃ nidhāya sā..
jagāma śayanaṃ tasya vadhārthaṃ varavarṇinī..6.78.50...
5.78.d:
अन्यस्मिन्दिवसे शस्त्रं सूक्ष्मं वेण्यां निधाय सा..
जगाम शयनं तस्य वधार्थं वरवर्णिनी..6.78.50...
5.78.m: On another day, concealing a small weapon in her braid of hair, / that fair woman went to his bed in order to kill him.

5.78.s:
tatastena samaṃ hāsyaṃ kṛtvā kṣatriyabhāvajam..
surataṃ rucirairbhāvairhāvairbhūribhireva ca ..51...
5.78.d:
ततस्तेन समं हास्यं कृत्वा क्षत्रियभावजम्..
सुरतं रुचिरैर्भावैर्हावैर्भूरिभिरेव च ..51...
5.78.m: Then, having laughed with him as befits a kṣatriya's nature, / [she engaged in] lovemaking with charming sentiments and many flirtatious gestures.

5.78.s:
tato nidrāvaśaṃ prāptaṃ taṃ nṛpaṃ sā nṛpapriyā ..
svaveṇyāḥ śastramādāya nijaghāna sunirdayā..52..
5.78.d:
ततो निद्रावशं प्राप्तं तं नृपं सा नृपप्रिया ..
स्ववेण्याः शस्त्रमादाय निजघान सुनिर्दया..52..
5.78.m: Then, when that king had fallen under the sway of sleep, that king's beloved, / taking the weapon from her braid, pitilessly struck him down.

5.78.s:
evaṃ tasya phalaṃ jātaṃ sadyastīrthasya bhaṃgajam ..
ānartādhipate raudraṃ sarvalokavigarhitam .. 53 ..
5.78.d:
एवं तस्य फलं जातं सद्यस्तीर्थस्य भंगजम् ..
आनर्ताधिपते रौद्रं सर्वलोकविगर्हितम् .. 53 ..
5.78.m: Thus immediately arose that terrible fruit, condemned by all the world, / resulting from the destruction of the tīrtha for the lord of Ānarta.

5.78.s:
adyāpi tatra deveśo rudraśīrṣaḥ sa tiṣṭhati ..
liṃgabhedabhayāttena na sa bhagno dvijottamāḥ ..54..
5.78.d:
अद्यापि तत्र देवेशो रुद्रशीर्षः स तिष्ठति ..
लिंगभेदभयात्तेन न स भग्नो द्विजोत्तमाः ..54..
5.78.m: Even today, that lord of the gods, Rudraśīrṣa, stands there; / it was not broken by him out of fear of breaking a liṅga, O best of brahmins.

5.78.s:
yastasya purataḥ sthitvā japedrudraśiraḥ śuciḥ ..
māghaśuklacaturdaśyāṃ pūjayitvā sragādibhiḥ ..55..
5.78.d:
यस्तस्य पुरतः स्थित्वा जपेद्रुद्रशिरः शुचिः ..
माघशुक्लचतुर्दश्यां पूजयित्वा स्रगादिभिः ..55..
5.78.m: Whoever, standing before it, purified, recites the Rudraśiras / on the fourteenth day of the bright fortnight of Māgha, after worshiping with garlands and other offerings,

5.78.s:
vāṃchitaṃ labhate cāśu tasyeśasya prabhāvataḥ..
aṣṭottaraśataṃ yāvadyo japetpurataḥ sthitaḥ .. 56 ..
5.78.d:
वांछितं लभते चाशु तस्येशस्य प्रभावतः..
अष्टोत्तरशतं यावद्यो जपेत्पुरतः स्थितः .. 56 ..
5.78.m: quickly obtains what is desired by the power of that Lord. / Whoever, standing before it, recites up to one hundred and eight times

5.78.s:
rudraśīrṣaṃ na saṃdehaḥ sa yāti paramāṃ gatim ..
ekavāraṃ naro yo vā tatpuraḥ paṭhati dvijaḥ .. 57 ..
5.78.d:
रुद्रशीर्षं न संदेहः स याति परमां गतिम् ..
एकवारं नरो यो वा तत्पुरः पठति द्विजः .. 57 ..
5.78.m: the Rudraśīrṣa, goes without doubt to the highest state; / or whatever man, a twice-born, recites it once before it,

5.78.s:
nityaṃ dinakṛtātpāpānmucyate dvijasattamāḥ ..
etadvaḥ sarvamākhyātaṃ rudraśīrṣasamudbhavam .. 58 ..
5.78.d:
नित्यं दिनकृतात्पापान्मुच्यते द्विजसत्तमाः ..
एतद्वः सर्वमाख्यातं रुद्रशीर्षसमुद्भवम् .. 58 ..
5.78.m: is freed from the sin committed on that day every day, O best of brahmins. / All this origin of Rudraśīrṣa has been recounted to you,

5.78.s:
māhātmyaṃ sarvapāpānāṃ sadyo nāśanakārakam..
maṃgalaṃ paramaṃ hyetadāyuṣyaṃ kīrtivardhanam..
rudraśīrṣasya māhātmyaṃ tasmācchrotavyamādarāt .. 59 ..
5.78.d:
माहात्म्यं सर्वपापानां सद्यो नाशनकारकम्..
मंगलं परमं ह्येतदायुष्यं कीर्तिवर्धनम्..
रुद्रशीर्षस्य माहात्म्यं तस्माच्छ्रोतव्यमादरात् .. 59 ..
5.78.m: a māhātmya that brings about the immediate destruction of all sins, / supremely auspicious, granting long life, and enhancing renown; / therefore, the māhātmya of Rudraśīrṣa should be heard with devotion.

5.78.s: iti śrīskānde mahāpurāṇa ekāśītisāhasryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ ṣaṣṭhe nāgarakhaṇḍe śrīhāṭakeśvarakṣetramāhātmye rudraśīrṣa (jāgeśvara )māhātmyavarṇanaṃnāmāṣṭasaptatitamo'dhyāyaḥ .. 78 .. .. dha ..
5.78.d: इति श्रीस्कान्दे महापुराण एकाशीतिसाहस्र्यां संहितायां षष्ठे नागरखण्डे श्रीहाटकेश्वरक्षेत्रमाहात्म्ये रुद्रशीर्ष (जागेश्वर )माहात्म्यवर्णनंनामाष्टसप्ततितमोऽध्यायः .. 78 .. .. ध ..
